title.zh: 卷一百二十 列傳第四十五 五王
title.raw: 卷一百二十 列傳第四十五 五王 Volume 120 Biographies 45: Five Kings

sentences.zh: ◎五王

translations.literal: ◎ The Five Kings
translations.idiomatic: ◎ The Five Kings

sentences.zh: 桓彥範，字士則，潤州丹陽人。

translations.literal: Huan Yanfan, styled Shize, was a native of Danyang in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yanfan, courtesy name Shize, was from Danyang in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以門蔭調右翊衛，遷司衛主簿。

translations.literal: Through yin privilege he was assigned to the Right Yiwu Guard and was promoted to chief clerk of the Directorate of Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he entered the Right Yiwu Guard and rose to chief clerk in the Directorate of Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑曰：「君之才，當自光大，毋恤於初。」

translations.literal: Di Renjie said: "Your talent ought to enlarge itself; do not worry about your early circumstances."
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie told him, "Your ability should grow great on its own; do not fret over modest beginnings."

sentences.zh: 厚為禮。

translations.literal: He treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He received him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 尋擢監察御史，遷累中丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to investigating censor and through successive appointments reached vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made investigating censor and, after several promotions, became vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 長安中，為司刑少卿。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he served as vice minister of justice in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chang'an period he held the post of vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 張昌宗引妖人迎占，言計不軌。

translations.literal: Zhang Changzong had engaged sorcerers for divination, and it was reported that his designs were not loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changzong brought in sorcerers for divination, and word spread that he was plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 宋璟請窮治其奸，武後以昌宗嘗自歸，不許。

translations.literal: Song Jing requested a thorough investigation of his treachery, but Empress Wu, because Changzong had once surrendered himself, would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing asked that his treachery be fully investigated, but because Changzong had once turned himself in, Empress Wu refused.

sentences.zh: 彥範諫曰：「昌宗謬橫恩，苞禍心，億測天命，皇神降怒，自擿其咎。

translations.literal: Yanfan remonstrated: "Changzong has wrongly received excessive favor, harbors a treacherous heart, presumptuously divines the Mandate of Heaven; the imperial spirits have sent down anger, and he has himself exposed his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan admonished: "Changzong has been showered with favor he does not deserve, nurses a treacherous heart, and dares to probe Heaven's mandate. The sacred powers are angry, and he has exposed his own guilt.

sentences.zh: 推原厥情，蓋防事暴之日得引首以免，未敗則候時為逆。

translations.literal: Tracing to the root of the matter, he likely wished to be able to offer his head to escape when affairs broke open; if not yet defeated, he would watch for the moment to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Looking to the root of his conduct, he surely meant to offer his head when matters exploded so as to escape punishment; if he had not yet failed, he would bide his time to rebel.

sentences.zh: 此兇詭之臣，營惑聖心。

translations.literal: This is a vicious and cunning minister who confuses the sage heart.
translations.idiomatic: He is a vicious, deceitful minister who bewilders Your Majesty's mind.

sentences.zh: 既自歸露，而尚與妖人祈福禳解，則果於必成，初無悔意。

translations.literal: Having already surrendered and exposed himself, yet still seeking blessings and exorcism with sorcerers shows he is resolved to succeed and from the first had no repentant intent.
translations.idiomatic: Though he has already confessed, he still seeks blessings and exorcism through sorcerers—proof that he is bent on success and never repented.

sentences.zh: 今而宥之，誠恐昌宗自謂應運，天下浩然從之。

translations.literal: If he is now pardoned, I truly fear Changzong will believe himself destined by fate, and all under Heaven will boldly follow him.
translations.idiomatic: If he is pardoned now, I fear Changzong will think himself Heaven's chosen, and the realm will rally to him in a rush.

sentences.zh: 父在，子稱尊為逆子；

translations.literal: When a father lives, for the son to claim superiority makes him a rebellious son;
translations.idiomatic: While a father lives, for a son to claim superiority is to be a rebellious son;

sentences.zh: 君在，臣圖位為逆臣。

translations.literal: when a ruler lives, for a minister to plot for position makes him a rebellious minister.
translations.idiomatic: while a ruler lives, for a minister to scheme for power is to be a rebellious minister.

sentences.zh: 逆而不誅，社稷懼亡。

translations.literal: Rebellion without execution—the altars of state may fear destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Treason left unpunished— the altars of state may be lost.

sentences.zh: 請付三司考治。」

translations.literal: I beg that he be handed over to the Three Offices for examination and punishment."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be handed to the Three Offices for trial and punishment."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: [The proposal] was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 時內史李嶠等屢奏：「往為酷吏破家者，請皆宥雪。」

translations.literal: At that time the palace secretary Li Qiao and others repeatedly memorialized: "Those whose families were ruined by harsh officials in the past should all be pardoned and cleared."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Secretary Li Qiao and others repeatedly petitioned: "All whose families were destroyed by cruel officials in the past should be pardoned and cleared."

sentences.zh: 依違未從。

translations.literal: [The emperor] hesitated and did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The throne wavered and did not agree.

sentences.zh: 彥範復上言：「自文明後得罪，惟揚、豫、博三州不免，它可悉赦。」

translations.literal: Yanfan memorialized again: "From after the Wensheng era those who offended should be amnestied, except that Yang, Yu, and Bo prefectures are not included; all others may be fully pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan submitted again: "All convicted since the Wensheng era may be pardoned, save those from Yang, Yu, and Bo prefectures; all others should receive a general amnesty."

sentences.zh: 疏十上，卒見聽。

translations.literal: He submitted ten memorials and in the end was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He sent up ten memorials and was finally heeded.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「大理，人命所縣，不可便辭詭合以自免。」

translations.literal: He once said: "The Court of Judicial Review is where human lives hang; one must not readily twist words and join sides to escape blame oneself."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "The Court of Judicial Review holds human lives in the balance; one must not twist words and trim one's views merely to save oneself."

sentences.zh: 上書戒帝曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial admonishing the emperor, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a memorial warning the emperor, saying:

sentences.zh: 《詩》以《關雎》為始，言後妃者人倫之本，治亂之端也。

translations.literal: The Odes begins with "Guan Ju"; speaking of empresses and consorts is the foundation of human relations and the source of order and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes opens with "Guan Ju"—on empresses and consorts rests the root of human relations and the turning point between order and chaos.

sentences.zh: 故舜之興以皇、英，而周之興以任、姒。

translations.literal: Thus in Shun's rise it was through E Huang and Nü Ying, and in Zhou's rise it was through Jiang of Ren and Si of Si.
translations.idiomatic: Shun rose through E Huang and Nü Ying; Zhou rose through Jiang of Ren and Si of Si.

sentences.zh: 桀奔南巢，禍階末嬉；

translations.literal: Jie fled to southern Nest; the disaster had its step in Mo Xi;
translations.idiomatic: Jie fled to Southern Nest—the calamity began with Mo Xi;

sentences.zh: 魯桓滅國，惑始齊姜。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Lu lost his state; bewitchment began with Jiang of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Lu lost his state—his ruin began with Lady Jiang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 伏見陛下臨朝視政，皇后必施帷殿上，預聞政事。

translations.literal: Humbly I observe that when Your Majesty holds court and governs, the empress invariably has a screen set up in the hall and participates in hearing administrative matters.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that whenever Your Majesty holds court, the empress sets up a screen in the hall and takes part in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂古王者謀及婦人，皆破國亡身，傾辀繼路。

translations.literal: Your servant is dull and considers that in antiquity kings who took counsel from women all ruined their states, lost their persons, and overturned their chariots one after another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is dull, but in antiquity every king who let women into his counsels ruined his state, lost his life, and left overturned chariots strewn along the road.

sentences.zh: 且以陰乘陽，違天也；

translations.literal: Moreover, for yin to ride upon yang violates Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: For yin to ride over yang is to violate Heaven;

sentences.zh: 以婦淩夫，違人也。

translations.literal: for a wife to tower over her husband violates human norms.
translations.idiomatic: for a wife to tower over her husband is to violate human norms.

sentences.zh: 違天不祥，違人不義。

translations.literal: To violate Heaven is inauspicious; to violate humanity is unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: To violate Heaven brings ill fortune; to violate humanity is unjust.

sentences.zh: 故《書》曰：「牝雞之晨，惟家之索。」

translations.literal: Thus the Documents says: "When the hen crows at dawn, that family is near ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Documents says: "When the hen crows at dawn, the household is near ruin."

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「無攸遂，在中饋。」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Nothing is to be pursued; stay within and provide food."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Nothing is to be pursued; remain within and provide food."

sentences.zh: 言婦人不得預外政也。

translations.literal: meaning that women must not intervene in external administration.
translations.idiomatic: —meaning that women must not meddle in public government.

sentences.zh: 伏願上以社稷為重，令皇后無居正殿，幹外朝，深居宮掖，修陰教以輔佐天子。

translations.literal: Humbly I wish that above all Your Majesty take the altars of state as weighty, command the empress not to sit in the main hall or meddle in the outer court, but dwell deep in the inner palace, cultivate feminine teaching to assist the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty put the altars of state first: let the empress leave the main hall, keep out of the outer court, dwell deep in the inner palace, and cultivate woman's teaching to support the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又道路籍籍，皆云胡僧慧範托浮屠法，詭惑後妃，出入禁奧，瀆撓朝政。

translations.literal: Further, on the roads there is rumor: "The Hu monk Hui Fan, under the guise of Buddhist law, beguiles the empress and consorts, enters and leaves the forbidden inner quarters, and profanes and disrupts court administration."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the roads are loud with rumor that the foreign monk Hui Fan, under cover of Buddhism, deceives the empress and consorts, enters the forbidden inner quarters, and profanes and disrupts the government.

sentences.zh: 陛下嘗輕騎微服，數幸其居，上下汙慢，君臣虧替。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has sometimes gone lightly on horse in plain dress, visiting his residence many times; above and below are defiled and negligent, ruler and minister suffer loss.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ridden out lightly in plain dress and visited his home again and again; high and low are stained with neglect, and the bond between ruler and minister is broken.

sentences.zh: 臣謂興化致治以康乂國家者，繇進善而棄惡。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that to raise the state to prosperity and order it for the peace of the family is done by advancing the good and abandoning evil.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that to lift the age, bring order, and give the state peace is to advance the good and cast out evil.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「執左道以亂政者殺，假鬼神以危人者殺。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Those who hold deviant ways to disturb government are to be put to death; those who borrow ghosts and spirits to endanger people are to be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Those who hold heterodox ways to disturb government should be killed; those who borrow ghosts and spirits to endanger others should be killed."

sentences.zh: 今慧範亂政危人者也，不急誅，且有變。

translations.literal: Hui Fan now disturbs government and endangers people; if he is not quickly executed, there will shortly be a change.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Fan now disturbs government and endangers the people. If he is not swiftly executed, trouble will follow.

sentences.zh: 除惡務本，願早裁之。

translations.literal: In removing evil one must strike at the root; I wish that he be cut off early.
translations.idiomatic: In rooting out evil one must strike at the source; I pray that he be cut down at once.

sentences.zh: 帝孱昏，狃左右，不能有所省納。

translations.literal: The emperor was feeble and dull, accustomed to those at his side, and could not be moved to heed and accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was weak and muddled, clinging to those around him, and could not be brought to listen.

sentences.zh: 俄墨敕以方士鄭普思為秘書監，葉靜能為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Before long a secret edict appointed the Daoist Zheng Pusi director of the Imperial Secretariat and Ye Jingneng director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a secret edict named the Daoist Zheng Pusi director of the Imperial Secretariat and Ye Jingneng director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 彥範執不可，帝曰：「要已用之，不可止。」

translations.literal: Yanfan objected that this could not be; the emperor said, "They have already been used; it cannot be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan held firm that this could not stand. The emperor said, "They are already in post; it cannot be undone."

sentences.zh: 彥範曰：「陛下始復位，制詔：『軍國皆用貞觀故事。』

translations.literal: Yanfan said: "When Your Majesty first restored the throne, an edict declared: 'All military and state affairs shall follow the precedents of the Zhenguan reign.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan said, "When Your Majesty first regained the throne, you decreed: 'All military and civil affairs shall follow Zhenguan precedent.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，以魏徵、虞世南、彥師古為監，以孔穎達為祭酒，如普思等方伎猥下，安足繼蹤前烈。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan period Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, and Yanshigu were directors and Kong Yingda was director of studies—how can men of low arts such as Pusi be adequate to follow in the footsteps of former worthies?
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan, Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, and Yanshigu were directors and Kong Yingda was director of studies. How can petty technicians like Pusi follow in the footsteps of such men?

sentences.zh: 臣恐物議謂陛下官不擇才，以天秩加私愛。」

translations.literal: Your servant fears public opinion will say Your Majesty appoints offices without selecting talent, adding private affection to heavenly offices."
translations.idiomatic: I fear the world will say Your Majesty appoints office without regard to talent, heaping private favor on Heaven's ranks."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時武三思以遷太后銜恚，慮不利諸武，而韋後雅為帝寵畏，且三思與蒸亂，由是朋讒奇中。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Sansi, nursing grievance over the relocation of the Empress Dowager, feared harm to the Wu clan; moreover Empress Wei was by nature beloved and feared by the emperor, and Sansi was moreover in illicit relations with her; therefore they joined as faction and slandered with peculiar success.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Sansi, bitter over the empress dowager's removal, feared for the Wu clan; Empress Wei was by nature both favored and feared by the emperor, and Sansi was also her illicit lover. They thus joined as a faction and their slanders struck home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷彥範等政事。

translations.literal: Before long, Yanfan and the others were removed from political affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yanfan and the others were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 五月，加特進，封扶陽郡王，賜姓韋，同後屬籍，錫金銀、錦繡，皆以鐵券恕十死，令朝朔望。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was given the special advance in rank, enfeoffed as Prince of Fuyang, granted the surname Wei and enrolled in the same clan register as the empress, bestowed gold, silver, and brocades, all with iron certificates forgiving ten deaths, and ordered to attend court on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was granted special advance in rank, enfeoffed as Prince of Fuyang, given the surname Wei and enrolled in the empress's clan register, showered with gold, silver, and brocade, each with an iron certificate forgiving ten capital offenses, and ordered to attend court on the first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 尋出為洺州刺史，改濠州。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as prefect of Luo Prefecture, then changed to Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as prefect of Luo, then transferred to Hao.

sentences.zh: 王同皎謀誅三思，事泄，三思誣彥範等同逆，陰令許州司功參軍鄭愔上變。

translations.literal: Wang Tongjiao plotted to kill Sansi; when the affair leaked, Sansi falsely accused Yanfan and the others of conspiring in rebellion, secretly ordering Zheng Yin, judicial secretary of Xu Prefecture, to report the treason.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tongjiao plotted to kill Sansi. When the plot leaked, Sansi accused Yanfan and the others of treason and secretly had Zheng Yin, judicial secretary of Xu Prefecture, report the crime.

sentences.zh: 乃貶彥範瀧州司馬，敬暉崖州司馬，袁恕己竇州司馬，崔玄暐白州司馬，張柬之新州司馬，悉奪勛封。

translations.literal: Then Yanfan was demoted to military commissioner of Long Prefecture, Jing Hui to Yai Prefecture, Yuan Shuji to Dou Prefecture, Cui Xuanwei to Bai Prefecture, Zhang Jianzhi to Xin Prefecture—all enfeoffments and honors were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan was demoted to military commissioner of Long, Jing Hui to Yai, Yuan Shuji to Dou, Cui Xuanwei to Bai, and Zhang Jianzhi to Xin; all honors and fiefs were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 三思又疏韋後隱穢，榜於道，請廢之。

translations.literal: Sansi again exposed the empress's hidden lewd conduct and posted it on the road, requesting her deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi again exposed the empress's secret misconduct and posted the account along the roads, asking that she be deposed.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，三思猥曰：「此殆彥範輩為。」

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken with rage; Sansi absurdly said: "This is nearly the work of Yanfan's faction."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Sansi said absurdly, "This is almost certainly Yanfan and his fellows."

sentences.zh: 命御史大夫李承嘉鞫狀，物色其人。

translations.literal: He ordered the censor-in-chief Li Chengjia to investigate and identify the culprits.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia to investigate and find the culprits.

sentences.zh: 承嘉即奏：「彥範、暉、柬之、恕己、玄暐暴訕搖變，內托廢後，而實危君。

translations.literal: Chengjia immediately reported: "Yanfan, Hui, Jianzhi, Shuji, and Xuanwei openly insult and sow disturbance, inwardly relying on deposing the empress while in truth endangering the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia at once reported: "Yanfan, Hui, Jianzhi, Shuji, and Xuanwei openly insult and stir unrest, using the plea to depose the empress while in truth endangering the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 人臣無將，當伏誅。」

translations.literal: As ministers without the proper attitude, they should submit to execution."
translations.idiomatic: As subjects who harbor rebellion, they deserve death."

sentences.zh: 詔有司議罪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the responsible offices to deliberate the crime.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the responsible offices to deliberate their punishment.

sentences.zh: 大理丞李朝隱執奏：「彥範等未訊即誅，恐為讎家誣蔑，請遣御史按實。」

translations.literal: The assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review Li Chaoyin held firm and reported: "Yanfan and the others have not yet been interrogated yet are to be executed—I fear enemies are falsely accusing them; I beg that censors be sent to verify the facts."
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director Li Chaoyin of the Court of Judicial Review held firm: "Yanfan and the others are to be executed without trial—I fear this is the work of enemies slandering them. I beg that censors be sent to verify the facts."

sentences.zh: 卿裴談請即誅斬，家籍沒。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Pei Tan requested immediate execution and confiscation of family property.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Pei Tan asked that they be executed at once and their families' property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 帝業嘗許以不死，遂流州，禁錮終身，子弟年十六以上謫徙嶺外。

translations.literal: The emperor had once promised they would not die; therefore they were exiled to distant prefectures, imprisoned for life, and sons and younger brothers sixteen and above were banished beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had once promised they would not die; they were therefore exiled to distant prefectures, imprisoned for life, and sons and younger brothers sixteen and older were banished beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 擢承嘉金紫光祿大夫、襄武郡公，後又賜彩五百段、錦被一。

translations.literal: Chengjia was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and made Duke of Xiangwu; later he was also given five hundred lengths of colored silk and one brocade quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and made Duke of Xiangwu; later he was also given five hundred lengths of colored silk and one brocade quilt.

sentences.zh: 進談刑部尚書，而貶朝隱。

translations.literal: Tan was promoted to minister of justice, while Chaoyin was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was promoted to Minister of Justice, while Chaoyin was demoted.

sentences.zh: 三思又諷節湣太子請夷彥範等三族，帝不從。

translations.literal: Sansi again prompted the Crown Prince of Jiemin to request the extermination of Yanfan's three clans; the emperor did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi again prompted Crown Prince Jiemin to ask that Yanfan's three clans be exterminated; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 三思慮五人者且復用，乃納崔湜計，遣周利貞矯制殺之。

translations.literal: Sansi feared the five would be employed again, and therefore adopted Cui Surong's plan, sending Zhou Lizhen with a forged edict to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi feared the five would be recalled to office and adopted Cui Surong's plan, sending Zhou Lizhen with a forged edict to kill them.

sentences.zh: 利貞至貴州，逢彥範，即縛曳竹槎上，肉盡，杖殺之，年五十四。

translations.literal: Lizhen reached Gui Prefecture and encountered Yanfan; he immediately bound him and dragged him on a bamboo raft until the flesh was gone and beat him to death—he was fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen reached Gui Prefecture and met Yanfan. He bound him at once, dragged him on a bamboo raft until the flesh was worn away, and beat him to death. Yanfan was fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，彥範等並追復官爵，賜實封二百戶，還其子孫，謚曰忠烈。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Yanfan and the others all had offices and titles posthumously restored, were granted two hundred households of permanent fief, their sons and grandsons were returned, and Yanfan received the posthumous name Zhonglie (Loyal and Fierce).
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Yanfan and the others had their offices and titles posthumously restored, were granted two hundred households of permanent fief, their sons and grandsons were returned, and Yanfan was given the posthumous name Loyal and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 開元六年，詔與暉、玄暐、柬之、恕己勤勞王家，皆配享中宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan an edict stated that because Hui, Xuanwei, Jianzhi, and Shuji had toiled for the royal house, they all received spirit tablets in Emperor Zhongzong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 6 (718) an edict declared that because Hui, Xuanwei, Jianzhi, and Shuji had labored for the royal house, they all received spirit tablets in Emperor Zhongzong's temple court.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，復贈彥範為司徒，暉太尉，玄暐太子太師，柬之司徒，恕己太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong Yanfan was posthumously made Situ again, Hui Grand Commandant, Xuanwei Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Jianzhi Situ, Shuji Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 3 (782) Yanfan was posthumously made Minister of Education again, Hui Grand Commandant, Xuanwei Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Jianzhi Minister of Education, and Shuji Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 彥範工屬文，然不甚喜觀書，所誌惟忠孝大略。

translations.literal: Yanfan was skillful at composition, yet he did not much enjoy reading books; what he recorded were only the great outlines of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan was skilled at writing, yet he did not much enjoy reading; what he set down were only the broad outlines of loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 居若不能言，及議論帝前，雖被詰讓，而安辭定色，辨色愈切。

translations.literal: In repose he seemed unable to speak, yet when debating before the emperor, though reproved and questioned, he kept a calm countenance and settled color, and his argument grew all the sharper.
translations.idiomatic: In private he seemed barely able to speak, yet when he argued before the emperor, though reproved and pressed, he kept a calm face and steady tone, and his pleading grew all the more urgent.

sentences.zh: 誅二張也，柬之勒兵景運門，將遂夷諸武。

translations.literal: When executing the two Zhangs, Jianzhi led troops at the Jingyun Gate and was about to exterminate all the Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When the two Zhangs were killed, Jianzhi led troops at the Jingyun Gate and was about to wipe out the entire Wu clan.

sentences.zh: 洛州長史薛季昶勸曰：「二兇雖誅，產、祿猶在，請除之。」

translations.literal: Xue Jichang, chief administrator of Luo Prefecture, urged: "The two villains are already killed, but Chansheng and Lu remain; I beg they be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jichang, chief administrator of Luo Prefecture, urged: "Though the two villains are dead, Chansheng and Lu remain. I beg that they be removed as well."

sentences.zh: 會日暮事遽，彥範不欲廣殺，因曰：「三思機上肉爾，留為天子藉手。」

translations.literal: As events were urgent at day's end, Yanfan did not wish to widen the killing and said: "Sansi is meat on the chopping block—leave him for the Son of Heaven's hand."
translations.idiomatic: But dusk came and events rushed on. Yanfan did not wish to widen the killing and said, "Sansi is meat on the block—leave him for the Son of Heaven to use."

sentences.zh: 委昶嘆曰：「吾無死所矣！」

translations.literal: Turning away, Jichang sighed: "I have nowhere to die now!"
translations.idiomatic: Jichang turned away and sighed, "I have nowhere left to die!"

sentences.zh: 俄而三思竊入宮，因韋後反盜朝權。

translations.literal: Before long Sansi stole into the palace, and through Empress Wei usurped court power in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sansi stole into the palace and, through Empress Wei, seized court power in turn.

sentences.zh: 同功者嘆曰：「死我者，桓君也。」

translations.literal: Those who had shared the achievement sighed: "The one who kills me is Lord Huan."
translations.idiomatic: Those who had shared in the deed sighed, "The one who will kill me is Lord Huan."

sentences.zh: 彥範亦曰：「主上昔為英王，故吾留武氏使自誅定。

translations.literal: Yanfan also said: "The sovereign was formerly Prince Ying; therefore I left the Wu to let them destroy themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan also said, "The sovereign was once Prince Ying; that is why I left the Wu clan to destroy themselves.

sentences.zh: 今大事已去，得非天乎！」

translations.literal: Now the great affair is gone—is this not Heaven's will?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the great affair is lost—is this not Heaven's will?"

sentences.zh: 初，將起事，告其母。

translations.literal: When they were about to rise in action, he told his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to act, he told his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「忠孝不並立，義先國家可也。」

translations.literal: His mother said: "Loyalty and filial piety cannot stand together; put righteousness to the state first—that is permissible."
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "Loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled; put the state's righteousness first—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 御史李福業者，嘗與彥範謀，及被殺，福業亦流番禺。

translations.literal: The censor Li Fuye had once plotted with Yanfan; when Yanfan was killed, Fuye was also exiled to Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Li Fuye had once plotted with Yanfan. When Yanfan was killed, Fuye was exiled to Panyu as well.

sentences.zh: 後亡匿吉州參軍敬元禮家，吏捕得，元禮俱坐死。

translations.literal: Later he went into hiding at the home of Jing Yuanli, a subordinate officer in Ji Prefecture; when officials captured him, Yuanli was jointly sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Later he hid in the home of Jing Yuanli, a subordinate officer in Ji Prefecture. When officials captured him, Yuanli was sentenced to death as well.

sentences.zh: 福業將刑，謝元禮曰：「子有親，吾甚愧恨。」

translations.literal: As Fuye was about to be executed, he apologized to Yuanli: "You have parents—I am deeply ashamed and regretful."
translations.idiomatic: As Fuye was about to be executed, he said to Yuanli in apology, "You have parents. I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 元禮曰：「公窮而歸我，我得已乎？」

translations.literal: Yuanli said: "You were in distress and came to me—how could I refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli said, "You were desperate and came to me. How could I turn you away?"

sentences.zh: 見者傷之。

translations.literal: Those who saw it were moved with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Those who witnessed it were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 時監察御史盧襲秀亦坐與桓、敬善，為冉祖雍所按，不屈。

translations.literal: At that time investigating censor Lu Xixiu was also implicated through friendship with Huan and Jing; he was investigated by Ran Zuyong and did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: At that time investigating censor Lu Xixiu was also implicated for his friendship with Huan and Jing. Investigated by Ran Zuyong, he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 或報曰：「南使至，桓、敬已死。」

translations.literal: Someone reported: "The southern envoy has arrived—Huan and Jing are already dead."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported, "The southern envoy has arrived. Huan and Jing are already dead."

sentences.zh: 襲秀泫然。

translations.literal: Xixiu shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Xixiu wept.

sentences.zh: 祖雍怒曰：「彥範等負國，君乃流涕。

translations.literal: Zuyong angrily said: "Yanfan and the others betrayed the state, yet you weep.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyong said angrily, "Yanfan and the others betrayed the state, yet you weep.

sentences.zh: 且君下獄，諸弟皆縱酒無憂色，何邪？」

translations.literal: Moreover, though you are in prison, your younger brothers all indulge in drink without worry—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, you are in prison, yet your younger brothers all drink freely without a care—why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「我何負哉？

translations.literal: He replied: "How have I failed?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "How have I failed?

sentences.zh: 正坐與彥範善耳。

translations.literal: It is only because I was friendly with Yanfan.
translations.idiomatic: It is only that I was friendly with Yanfan.

sentences.zh: 今盡殺諸弟則已，如獨殺襲秀，恐公不得高枕而瞑！」

translations.literal: If you kill all my brothers, so be it; but if you kill only Xixiu alone, I fear you will not be able to rest your head on a high pillow!"
translations.idiomatic: If you kill all my brothers, so be it. But if you kill only me, I fear you will not sleep easily!"

sentences.zh: 祖雍色動，握其手曰：「當活公。」

translations.literal: Zuyong's expression changed; he grasped his hand and said: "I shall let you live."
translations.idiomatic: Zuyong's expression changed. He took his hand and said, "I shall let you live."

sentences.zh: 遂得不坐。

translations.literal: Thus he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 襲秀者，其祖方慶，武德中，為察非掾，秦王器之。

translations.literal: As for Xixiu, his grandfather was Fang Qing, who in the Wude era served as an investigator of irregularities and was valued by Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Xixiu's grandfather Fang Qing, in the Wude era, served as an investigator of irregularities and won the esteem of the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 嘗引與議建成事，方慶辭曰：「母老矣，丐身歸養。」

translations.literal: He once summoned him to discuss the affair of Li Jiancheng; Fang Qing declined, saying: "My mother is old; I beg leave to return and support her."
translations.idiomatic: The prince once summoned him to discuss the affair of Li Jiancheng. Fang Qing declined: "My mother is old; I beg leave to go home and care for her."

sentences.zh: 王不逼也。

translations.literal: The prince did not press him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince did not press him.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，為稿城令。」

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was magistrate of Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era he served as magistrate of Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 彥範弟玄範，官至常州刺史；

translations.literal: Yanfan's younger brother Xuanfan rose to prefect of Chang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan's younger brother Xuanfan rose to prefect of Chang;

sentences.zh: 臣範，工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Chenfan, vice minister in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Chenfan became vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 薛季昶者，絳州龍門人。

translations.literal: Xue Jichang was a native of Longmen in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jichang was from Longmen in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武後時上書，自布衣擢監察御史，以累左遷平遙尉，復拜御史。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time he submitted a memorial and was raised from commoner to investigating censor; through involvement in a case he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Pingyao, then again appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he submitted a memorial and was raised from commoner to investigating censor. After involvement in a case he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Pingyao, then appointed censor again.

sentences.zh: 屢按獄如旨，擢給事中。

translations.literal: He repeatedly handled cases as the throne wished and was promoted to attendant within the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly handled cases to the throne's liking and was promoted to attendant within the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 夏官郎中侯味虛將兵討契丹，不利，妄言「賊行有蛇虎導軍」。

translations.literal: Hou Weixu, director of the summer office, led troops against the Khitan without success and falsely claimed: "As the bandits march, serpents and tigers guide the army."
translations.idiomatic: Hou Weixu of the Ministry of War led troops against the Khitan without success and falsely claimed, "Serpents and tigers guide the enemy army as it marches."

sentences.zh: 後惡其詭，拜季昶為河北道按察使。

translations.literal: Later, detesting his deceit, [the court] appointed Jichang investigating commissioner of the Hebei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Later, detesting his deceit, the court appointed Jichang investigating commissioner of the Hebei circuit.

sentences.zh: 季昶馳至軍，斬味虛以聞，威震北方。

translations.literal: Jichang galloped to the army, beheaded Weixu and reported it; his authority shook the north.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang galloped to the army, beheaded Weixu, and reported it. His authority shook the north.

sentences.zh: 稿城尉吳澤射殺驛使，髡民女發為髢，州不能劾，季昶杖殺之。

translations.literal: Wu Ze, assistant magistrate of Gaocheng, shot and killed a courier, shaved a commoner's daughter and made her hair into a wig; the prefecture could not prosecute him, and Jichang beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ze, assistant magistrate of Gaocheng, shot and killed a courier, shaved a commoner's daughter, and made a wig from her hair. The prefecture could not prosecute him, so Jichang beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 然後布恩信，甄表善良。

translations.literal: Only then did he spread kindness and trust and select and commend the good.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he spread kindness and trust and commend the worthy.

sentences.zh: 或傳季昶曩為味虛笞辱，故深文報怨。

translations.literal: Some reported that Jichang had once been flogged and humiliated by Weixu, and therefore piled on charges to repay the grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Jichang had once been flogged and humiliated by Weixu and therefore piled on charges to settle the score.

sentences.zh: 自給事中數月為御史中丞，坐事左遷。

translations.literal: Within a few months from attendant he became vice censor-in-chief; through involvement in a case he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he rose from attendant to vice censor-in-chief, then was demoted after involvement in a case.

sentences.zh: 久乃入為雍州長史，遷文昌左衛，為洛州長史。

translations.literal: After a long time he entered the capital as chief administrator of Yong Prefecture, was transferred to the Left Guard of Wenchang, and became chief administrator of Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he entered the capital as chief administrator of Yong Prefecture, was transferred to the Left Guard of Wenchang, and became chief administrator of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 預誅易之等功，進戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: For his part in killing Yizhi and the others he was advanced to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in killing the Zhang brothers he was promoted to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 五王失柄，出季昶荊州長史，貶儋州司馬。

translations.literal: When the Five Kings lost power, Jichang was sent out as chief administrator of Jing Prefecture and demoted to military commissioner of Dan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Kings lost power, Jichang was sent out as chief administrator of Jing and demoted to military commissioner of Dan.

sentences.zh: 初，季昶與昭州首領周慶立、廣州事馬光楚客不葉，懼二怨，不敢往。

translations.literal: Earlier Jichang had been on bad terms with Zhou Qingli, chief of Zha Prefecture, and Ma Guangchu, administrator of Guang Prefecture; fearing their two grudges, he dared not go.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jichang had been on bad terms with Zhou Qingli of Zha Prefecture and Ma Guangchu of Guang Prefecture. Fearing their enmity, he dared not go.

sentences.zh: 嘆曰：「吾至是邪！」

translations.literal: He sighed: "Have I come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "Have I come to this!"

sentences.zh: 即具棺沐浴，仰藥死。

translations.literal: He immediately prepared his coffin, bathed, took poison, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He at once prepared his coffin, bathed, took poison, and died.

sentences.zh: 葬昭州。

translations.literal: He was buried in Zha Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in Zha Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，詔贈左御史大夫，同彥稾等賜一子官。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Left Censor-in-Chief and, like Yanfan and the others, granted one son an office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Left Censor-in-Chief and, like Yanfan and the others, granted one son an office.

sentences.zh: 季昶剛烈，然喜入先語以為實，後雖有辨理，不能得也。

translations.literal: Jichang was fierce and stern, yet he liked to accept the first account as true; though later there might be reasoned argument, he could not be won over.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang was fierce and stern, yet he tended to accept the first account as true; even when later argument showed otherwise, he could not be moved.

sentences.zh: 而敦愛故舊，禮有名士，其長可蓋所缺雲。

translations.literal: Yet he was warm in affection toward old friends and treated famous scholars with courtesy; his strengths could cover his shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was warm toward old friends and courteous to famous scholars; his strengths could cover his shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 楊元琰者，字溫，虢州閺鄉人，漢太尉震十八代孫。

translations.literal: Yang Yuanyan, styled Wen, was a native of Min Township in Guo Prefecture, eighteenth-generation descendant of Yang Zhen, Grand Commandant of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuanyan, courtesy name Wen, was from Min Township in Guo Prefecture, eighteenth-generation descendant of Han Grand Commandant Yang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 生數歲未言，相者視曰：「語遲者神定，必為重器。」

translations.literal: For several years after birth he did not speak; a physiognomist looked at him and said: "One who speaks late has a settled spirit and will surely become a great vessel."
translations.idiomatic: For several years after birth he did not speak. A physiognomist looked at him and said, "One who speaks late has a settled spirit and will surely become a great man."

sentences.zh: 及長，秀眉美須髯，崇肩博頤。

translations.literal: When grown, he had elegant brows, a fine beard, high shoulders, and a broad jaw.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he had elegant brows, a fine beard, high shoulders, and a broad jaw.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，七日不食。

translations.literal: During his father's mourning he did not eat for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: During his father's mourning he fasted for seven days.

sentences.zh: 服除，補梓州參軍，平棘令，課第一，御史府表其政，璽書褒厲。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed military adjutant in Zi Prefecture and magistrate of Pingji; his assessment ranked first, the censorate commended his administration, and an imperial edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he served as military adjutant in Zi Prefecture and magistrate of Pingji. His assessment ranked first, the censorate commended his administration, and an imperial edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 再擢永寧軍副使，忤用事者免。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to deputy commissioner of the Yongning Army; offending those in power, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice promoted to deputy commissioner of the Yongning Army, but offended those in power and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 載初中，為安南副都護，三徙為荊府長史，五遷州刺史，鹹有風績。

translations.literal: In the early Zaichu era he was vice protector-general of Annan, was transferred three times to chief administrator of Jing Prefecture, and was promoted five times to prefect—all with distinguished conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zaichu era he was vice protector-general of Annan, was transferred three times to chief administrator of Jing, and was promoted five times to prefect—each post marked by distinguished conduct.

sentences.zh: 初，張柬之代為荊州，共乘艫江中，私語外家革命，元琰悲涕慷慨，誌在王室。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Jianzhi replaced him in Jing Prefecture, they shared a boat on the river and privately spoke of the revolution of the maternal clan; Yuanyan wept with grief and passion, his will fixed on the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Jianzhi replaced him in Jing, they shared a boat on the river and spoke privately of overthrowing the Wu clan. Yuanyan wept with grief and passion, his heart set on the royal house.

sentences.zh: 柬之執政，故引為右羽林將軍，謂曰：「江上之言，君叵忘之，今可以勉！」

translations.literal: When Jianzhi took power he therefore brought him in as general of the Right Yulin Guard and said: "What was said on the river—you must not forget it; now you can strive!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jianzhi took power he brought him in as general of the Right Yulin Guard and said, "What was said on the river—you must not forget it. Now you can act!"

sentences.zh: 乃與李多祚等定計斬二張。

translations.literal: He then joined Li Duozuo and others in planning to behead the two Zhangs.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Li Duozuo and others in planning to kill the two Zhang brothers.

sentences.zh: 進雲麾將軍，封弘農郡公，實封戶五百，賜鐵券恕十死。

translations.literal: He was advanced to general of the Cloud-Banner Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong with five hundred households of permanent fief, and granted an iron certificate forgiving ten deaths.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the Cloud-Banner Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong with five hundred households of permanent fief, and granted an iron certificate forgiving ten capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 敬暉等為武三思所構，元琰知禍未已，乃詭計請祝髮事浮屠，悉還官封。

translations.literal: Jing Hui and the others were framed by Wu Sansi; Yuanyan knew disaster was not ended and therefore used a stratagem, asking to shave his head and serve the Buddha, returning all offices and enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hui and the others were framed by Wu Sansi. Yuanyan knew the danger was not over and therefore devised a stratagem, asking to shave his head and become a monk, returning all offices and enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 中宗不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong refused.

sentences.zh: 暉聞，尚戲曰：「胡頭應祝。」

translations.literal: When Hui heard, he still jested: "The Hu head ought to be tonsured."
translations.idiomatic: When Hui heard, he still jested, "That Hu head ought to be tonsured."

sentences.zh: 以多鬛似胡雲。

translations.literal: because his thick beard resembled a Hu.
translations.idiomatic: —because his thick beard made him look like a foreigner.

sentences.zh: 元琰曰：「功成不退，懼亡。

translations.literal: Yuanyan said: "Merit achieved without withdrawal—I fear destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyan said, "Merit achieved without withdrawal—I fear ruin.

sentences.zh: 我不空言。」

translations.literal: I do not speak in vain."
translations.idiomatic: I do not speak in vain."

sentences.zh: 暉感之，然已不及計。

translations.literal: Hui was moved, yet it was already too late to plan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was moved, but it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 暉等死，獨元琰全。

translations.literal: When Hui and the others died, Yuanyan alone was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui and the others died, Yuanyan alone survived unscathed.

sentences.zh: 再遷衛尉卿，又上官封，願追寵其親，帝哀憐，贈越州都督長史。

translations.literal: He was twice transferred to minister of the court of imperial regalia; on another occasion he memorialized, wishing posthumous honors for his parents; the emperor pitied him and posthumously made his father chief administrator under the protector-general of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice transferred to minister of the court of imperial regalia. On another occasion he memorialized to honor his parents posthumously; the emperor took pity and posthumously made his father chief administrator under the protector-general of Yue.

sentences.zh: 李多祚死太子難，元琰坐厚善，系獄，蕭至忠救之，免。

translations.literal: When Li Duozuo died in the crown prince's difficulty, Yuanyan was implicated for close friendship, imprisoned; Xiao Zhizhong rescued him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Duozuo died in the crown prince's rebellion, Yuanyan was implicated for their close friendship and imprisoned. Xiao Zhizhong rescued him and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，數上書乞骸骨，不聽。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; he was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he repeatedly asked to retire; the throne would not listen.

sentences.zh: 四遷刑部尚書，封魏國公。

translations.literal: Through four promotions he became minister of justice and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Through four promotions he became Minister of Justice and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 徙太子賓客，詔設位東宮，太子為拜。

translations.literal: He was moved to mentor of the heir apparent; an edict ordered a seat set in the Eastern Palace, and the crown prince bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was made mentor of the heir apparent; an edict ordered a seat set in the Eastern Palace, and the crown prince bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 俄致仕。

translations.literal: Soon he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 開元六年卒，年七十九，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Kaiyuan at age seventy-nine; his posthumous name was Zhong (Loyal).
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kaiyuan 6 (718) at seventy-nine; his posthumous name was Loyal.

sentences.zh: 生平無留蓄，中外食其家常數十人。

translations.literal: Throughout his life he kept no savings; inside and outside his household, several tens ate at his table.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life he kept no savings; several dozen people inside and outside his household ate at his table.

sentences.zh: 臨終，敕諸子薄葬。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he ordered his sons to bury him simply.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he ordered his sons to give him a simple burial.

sentences.zh: 子仲昌，字蔓。

translations.literal: His son Zhongchang, styled Man.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongchang, courtesy name Man.

sentences.zh: 以通經為修文生。

translations.literal: Through mastery of the classics he became a Xiucheng student.
translations.idiomatic: Through mastery of the classics he became a Xiucheng student.

sentences.zh: 累調，不甚顯。

translations.literal: Through successive appointments he was not very prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive appointments he did not rise very high.

sentences.zh: 以河陽尉對策，玄宗擢第一，授蒲州法曹參軍，判入異等，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: As assistant magistrate of Heyang he answered policy questions; Xuanzong ranked him first, appointed him legal adjutant in Pu Prefecture, judged his work exceptional, and promoted him to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: As assistant magistrate of Heyang he answered policy questions. Emperor Xuanzong ranked him first, appointed him legal adjutant in Pu Prefecture, judged his work exceptional, and promoted him to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 坐累為孝義令。

translations.literal: Through involvement in a case he became magistrate of Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: After involvement in a case he became magistrate of Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 鸞降庭樹，太守蕭恕表其政，徙下邽。

translations.literal: A phoenix alighted on a tree in his courtyard; Prefect Xiao Shu memorialized his administration, and he was transferred to Xiaji.
translations.idiomatic: A phoenix alighted on a tree in his courtyard. Prefect Xiao Shu memorialized his administration, and he was transferred to Xiaji.

sentences.zh: 終吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He ended as director in the Ministry of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as director in the Ministry of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 仲昌資長於吏。

translations.literal: Zhongchang's talent lay in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchang's talent lay in administration.

sentences.zh: 常分父邑租振宗黨。

translations.literal: He often divided his father's fief rent to relieve the clan.
translations.idiomatic: He often divided his father's fief rent to support the clan.

sentences.zh: 禦身以約，善與人交，士樂從之遊雲。

translations.literal: He restrained himself through frugality, was good at making friends, and gentlemen gladly followed him in company.
translations.idiomatic: He lived frugally, made friends easily, and gentlemen gladly kept his company.

sentences.zh: 敬暉，字仲曄，絳州平陽人。

translations.literal: Jing Hui, styled Zhongye, was a native of Pingyang in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hui, courtesy name Zhongye, was from Pingyang in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉明經。

translations.literal: At age twenty he passed the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，為衛州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shengli era he was prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shengli era he was prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 是時，河北經突厥所騷，方秋而城，暉曰：「金湯非粟不守，豈有棄農畝，事池隍哉？」

translations.literal: At that time Hebei had been harassed by the Turks; it was autumn and they were building walls. Hui said: "Walls and moats cannot be held without grain—how can one abandon the fields to tend moats and ramparts?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hebei had been harassed by the Turks. It was autumn and the people were building walls. Hui said, "Walls and moats cannot be held without grain—how can we abandon the fields to tend ramparts?"

sentences.zh: 縱民歸斂，闔部賴安。

translations.literal: He let the people return to harvest; the whole prefecture relied on him for peace.
translations.idiomatic: He let the people return to harvest, and the whole prefecture found peace through him.

sentences.zh: 遷夏官侍郎，出為太州刺史，改洛陽長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the summer office, sent out as prefect of Tai Prefecture, then changed to chief administrator of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the summer office, sent out as prefect of Tai, then made chief administrator of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 武後幸長安，為副留守，以治幹聞，璽書勞之，多賜物段。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu visited Chang'an he served as deputy defender; known for administrative ability, he received an imperial edict of commendation and many lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu visited Chang'an he served as deputy defender. Known for administrative ability, he received an imperial edict of commendation and many gifts of silk.

sentences.zh: 長安二年，授中臺右丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an he was appointed right vice director of the central secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an 2 (702) he was appointed right vice director of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以誅二張功，加金紫光祿大夫，為侍中、平陽郡公，實封五百戶，進封齊國。

translations.literal: For his merit in killing the two Zhangs he was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, made attendant-in-chief and Duke of Pingyang with five hundred households of permanent fief, and advanced to Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: For killing the two Zhang brothers he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, attendant-in-chief, and Duke of Pingyang with five hundred households of permanent fief, then advanced to Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 暉表請諸武王者宜悉降爵，繇是皆為公。

translations.literal: Hui memorialized that all those enfeoffed as kings of the Wu should have their titles reduced; thereby they all became dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Hui memorialized that all Wu princes should have their titles reduced; thereby they all became dukes.

sentences.zh: 三思憤。

translations.literal: Sansi was furious.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi was furious.

sentences.zh: 俄封平陽郡王，加特進罷政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyang, given special advance in rank, and removed from political affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyang, given special advance in rank, and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 初，易之已誅，薛季昶請收諸武，暉亦苦諫，不從。

translations.literal: When Yizhi had already been killed, Xue Jichang requested that all the Wu be seized; Hui also remonstrated bitterly, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi had been killed, Xue Jichang asked that the entire Wu clan be seized. Hui also remonstrated bitterly, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 三思濁亂，暉每椎坐悵恨，彈指流血。

translations.literal: Sansi was corrupt and disorderly; Hui would each time pound the seat in grief and regret, snapping his fingers until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi was corrupt and disorderly. Hui would pound the seat in grief, snapping his fingers until blood flowed.

sentences.zh: 尋及貶，又放瓊州，為周利貞所害。

translations.literal: Before long he was demoted and again exiled to Qiong Prefecture, where Zhou Lizhen killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted and exiled to Qiong, where Zhou Lizhen killed him.

sentences.zh: 睿宗時，追復官爵，又贈秦州都督，謚曰肅湣。

translations.literal: In Ruizong's time his offices and titles were posthumously restored, and he was also made protector-general of Qin Prefecture; his posthumous name was Sumi (Solemn and Lamented).
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ruizong his offices and titles were posthumously restored, and he was made protector-general of Qin; his posthumous name was Solemn and Lamented.

sentences.zh: 崔玄暐，博陵安平人，本名畢，武後時，有所避，改焉。

translations.literal: Cui Xuanwei was a native of Anping in Boling; his original name was Bi; in Empress Wu's time he changed it to avoid something.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanwei was from Anping in Boling. His original name was Bi; under Empress Wu he changed it to avoid a taboo.

sentences.zh: 少以學行稱，叔父秘書少監行功器之。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed for learning and conduct; his uncle, Vice Director of the Secretariat Xing Gong, valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was famed for learning and conduct. His uncle, Vice Director of the Secretariat Xing Gong, valued him.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，為高陵主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and became chief clerk of Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and became chief clerk of Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 居父喪盡禮。

translations.literal: During his father's mourning he fulfilled all rites.
translations.idiomatic: During his father's mourning he fulfilled every rite.

sentences.zh: 廬有燕，更巢共乳。

translations.literal: At his mourning hut swallows nested; they changed nests and nursed together.
translations.idiomatic: At his mourning hut swallows nested; they changed nests and nursed their young together.

sentences.zh: 母盧，有賢操，常戒玄暐曰：「吾聞姨兄辛玄馭云：『子姓仕宦，有言其貧窶不自存，此善也；

translations.literal: His mother Lu had worthy conduct and often admonished Xuanwei: "I heard my cousin's husband Xin Xuanyu say: 'When sons and clansmen enter office, if people say they are poor and cannot support themselves, that is good;
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Lu was virtuous and often warned Xuanwei: "I heard my cousin's husband Xin Xuanyu say, 'When sons and clansmen enter office, if people say they are poor and cannot support themselves, that is good;

sentences.zh: 若貲貨盈衍，惡也。』

translations.literal: if goods and wealth overflow, that is evil.
translations.idiomatic: if goods and wealth overflow, that is evil.

sentences.zh: 吾嘗以為確論。

translations.literal: I have always held this a sound doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: I have always held this a sound doctrine.

sentences.zh: 比見親表仕者務多財以奉親，而親不究所從來。

translations.literal: Lately I see kinsmen in office striving for much wealth to support their parents, while the parents do not investigate whence it comes.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I see kinsmen in office striving for wealth to support their parents, while the parents do not ask where it comes from.

sentences.zh: 必出於祿稟則善，如其不然，何異盜乎？

translations.literal: If it must come from salary and grain stipends, that is good; if not, how is it different from theft?
translations.idiomatic: If it comes from salary and stipends, that is good. If not, how is it different from theft?

sentences.zh: 若今為吏，不能忠清，無以戴天履地。

translations.literal: If you now become an official and cannot be loyal and pure, you have no way to bear Heaven on your head or tread Earth under your feet.
translations.idiomatic: If you now become an official and cannot be loyal and pure, you have no way to face Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 宜識吾意。」

translations.literal: You should understand my meaning."
translations.idiomatic: You should understand what I mean."

sentences.zh: 故玄暐所守以清白名。

translations.literal: Therefore what Xuanwei upheld won him a name for purity.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Xuanwei upheld himself and won a name for integrity.

sentences.zh: 母亡，哀毀，甘露降庭樹。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was devastated with grief; sweet dew fell on the trees in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was devastated with grief; sweet dew fell on the trees in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 後久疾，宰相不召見者累月。

translations.literal: Later Empress Wu was long ill and did not summon the chief ministers for many months.
translations.idiomatic: Later Empress Wu was long ill and did not summon the chief ministers for many months.

sentences.zh: 及少閑，玄暐奏言：「皇太子、相王皆仁明孝友，宜侍醫藥，不宜引異姓出入禁闥。」

translations.literal: When she had a little respite, Xuanwei memorialized: "The crown prince and the Prince of Xiang are all benevolent, bright, filial, and friendly; they should attend her with medicine, and unrelated surnames should not be brought in and out of the forbidden gates."
translations.idiomatic: When she had a little respite, Xuanwei memorialized: "The crown prince and the Prince of Xiang are benevolent, bright, filial, and friendly. They should attend her with medicine. Unrelated persons should not be brought in and out of the forbidden gates."

sentences.zh: 後慰納。

translations.literal: The empress was comforted and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was comforted and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 以誅二張功為中書令、博陵郡公。

translations.literal: For his merit in killing the two Zhangs he was made director of the Secretariat and Duke of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: For killing the two Zhang brothers he was made Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 後遷上陽宮，顧玄暐曰：「諸臣進皆因人，而雲暐我所擢，何至是？」

translations.literal: Later she moved to the Shangyang Palace and turned to Xuanwei, saying: "All the ministers who advanced did so through others, yet they say Xuanwei was raised by me—how could it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Later she moved to the Shangyang Palace and turned to Xuanwei, saying, "All the ministers who advanced did so through others, yet they say you were raised by me—how could it come to this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此正所以報陛下也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "This is precisely how I repay Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "This is precisely how I repay Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 俄拜博陵郡王，罷政事，冊其妻為妃，賜實封五百戶，檢校益州大都督府長史，知都督事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Prince of Boling, removed from political affairs, his wife was enfeoffed as consort, granted five hundred households of permanent fief, made acting chief administrator of the Great Protectorate of Yi Prefecture, and given charge of protector affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Prince of Boling, dismissed from office, his wife was enfeoffed as consort, granted five hundred households of permanent fief, and made acting chief administrator of Yi with charge of protector affairs.

sentences.zh: 會貶，又流古州。

translations.literal: When demoted, he was again exiled to Gu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When demoted, he was exiled again to Gu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道病卒，年六十九，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: He died of illness on the road at age sixty-nine; his posthumous name was Wenxian (Cultured and Meritorious).
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness on the road at sixty-nine; his posthumous name was Cultured and Meritorious.

sentences.zh: 玄暐三世不異居，家人怡怡如也。

translations.literal: For three generations the Xuanwei family did not live apart; the household was harmonious and content.
translations.idiomatic: For three generations the Xuanwei family lived together; the household was harmonious and content.

sentences.zh: 貧寓郊墅，群從皆自遠會食，無它爨，與昇尤友愛。

translations.literal: Poor, they lodged in a suburban villa; all the clan came from afar to eat together with no other cooking, and he was especially affectionate with Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, they lodged in a suburban villa. The whole clan came from afar to eat together with no other cooking, and he was especially close to Sheng.

sentences.zh: 族人貧孤者，撫養教勵。

translations.literal: Clansmen who were poor and orphaned he nurtured, taught, and encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: He nurtured, taught, and encouraged clansmen who were poor and orphaned.

sentences.zh: 後雖秉權，而子弟仕進不使逾常資，當時稱重。

translations.literal: Later, though he held power, he did not let sons and younger brothers advance beyond ordinary qualifications in office; the age praised his weight.
translations.idiomatic: Later, though he held power, he did not let his sons and younger brothers advance beyond ordinary qualifications; the age respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 少頗屬辭，晚以非己長，不復構思，專意經術。

translations.literal: In youth he was quite literary, but in later years, finding it not his strength, he no longer composed and devoted himself to classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he wrote well, but in later years, finding it not his strength, he stopped composing and devoted himself to classical learning.

sentences.zh: 子璩，亦有文。

translations.literal: His son Qu also had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qu was also a capable writer.

sentences.zh: 開元二年詔：「玄暐、柬之，神龍之初，保乂王室，奸臣忌焉，謫歿荒海，流落變遷，感激忠義。

translations.literal: An edict of the second year of Kaiyuan stated: "Xuanwei and Jianzhi, at the beginning of Shenlong, preserved and comforted the royal house; treacherous ministers envied them, and they were demoted and died in the wild sea, drifting through change, moved by loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of Kaiyuan 2 (714) stated: "Xuanwei and Jianzhi, at the beginning of Shenlong, preserved the royal house. Treacherous ministers envied them; they were demoted and died in exile, drifting through change, moved by loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 宜以玄暐子璩、柬之孫毖，並為朝散大夫。」

translations.literal: Xuanwei's son Qu and Jianzhi's grandson Bi should both be made Grand Masters of Palace Leisure."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwei's son Qu and Jianzhi's grandson Bi should both be made Grandees of Palace Leisure."

sentences.zh: 璩終禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Qu ended as vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Qu ended his career as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 璩子渙。

translations.literal: Qu's son Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Qu's son was Huan.

sentences.zh: 渙博綜經術，長論議。

translations.literal: Huan was broadly versed in classical learning and excelled at discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was broadly versed in the classics and excelled at discourse.

sentences.zh: 十歲居父喪，毀辟加人，陸元方異之。

translations.literal: At ten he observed his father's mourning and was more devastated than others; Lu Yuanfang regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he observed his father's mourning with grief beyond others; Lu Yuanfang regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 起家亳州司功參軍，還調。

translations.literal: He began as legal adjutant in Bo Prefecture and returned for reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: He began as legal adjutant in Bo Prefecture and returned for reassignment.

sentences.zh: 於是入判者千餘，吏部侍郎嚴挺之施特榻試《彜尊銘》，謂曰：「子清廟器，故以題相命。」

translations.literal: More than a thousand entered for judgment; Vice Minister of Civil Office Yan Tingzhi set a special couch and tested him on the "Yi Zun Inscription," saying: "You are a vessel for the pure temple; therefore I set this topic as your charge."
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand entered for judgment. Vice Minister Yan Tingzhi set a special couch and tested him on the "Yi Zun Inscription," saying, "You are a vessel fit for the temple; therefore I set this topic for you."

sentences.zh: 累遷司門員外郎。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became vice director of the gate office.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he became vice director of the gate office.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠惡不附己，出為巴西太守。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong hated those who did not attach to him and sent him out as prefect of Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong hated those who would not attach to him and sent him out as prefect of Baxi.

sentences.zh: 玄宗西狩，迎謁於道。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong went west on campaign, Huan met and paid homage on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong fled west, Huan met and paid homage on the road.

sentences.zh: 帝見占奏，以為明治體，恨得之晚，房琯亦薦之，即日拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor saw his prognostications and memorials, considered him clear on governing principles, regretted obtaining him late; Fang Guan also recommended him, and the same day he was made vice director of the Secretariat and joint manager of affairs with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw his prognostications and memorials, judged him clear on governing principles, and regretted finding him so late. Fang Guan also recommended him, and the same day he was made vice director of the Secretariat and joint manager of affairs.

sentences.zh: 肅宗立，與韋見素等同赴行在。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, he went with Wei Jiansu and others to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, he went with Wei Jiansu and others to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 時京師未復，舉選不至，詔渙為江淮宣諭選補使。

translations.literal: At that time the capital had not been recovered and selections did not arrive; an edict made Huan commissioner for proclaiming and selecting replacements in Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the capital had not been recovered and selections did not arrive. An edict made Huan commissioner for proclaiming and selecting replacements in Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 收采遺逸，不以親故自嫌。

translations.literal: He gathered and selected the overlooked and did not shrink from kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered overlooked talent and did not shrink from appointing kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「仰才虞謗，吾不忍為。」

translations.literal: He often said: "To rely on talent and fear slander—I cannot bear to do that."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "To rely on talent and fear slander—I cannot bear to do that."

sentences.zh: 然聽受不甚精，以不職罷為左散騎常侍，兼餘杭太守、江東采訪防禦使。

translations.literal: Yet his hearing and acceptance were not very precise; for dereliction of duty he was dismissed as left regular attendant and concurrently made prefect of Yuhang and Jiangdong investigating and defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his judgment was not very precise. For dereliction of duty he was dismissed as left regular attendant and concurrently made prefect of Yuhang and Jiangdong investigating and defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入遷吏部侍郎、集賢院待制。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was transferred to vice minister of civil office and attendant at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital and was transferred to vice minister of civil office and attendant at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 簡淡自處，時望尤重。

translations.literal: Simple and restrained in his conduct, he was especially esteemed by public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Simple and restrained in his conduct, he was especially esteemed.

sentences.zh: 遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 元載輔政，與中官董秀槃結固寵，渙疾之，因進見，慨然論載奸。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai assisted in government and, with the eunuch Dong Xiu, wove bonds to secure favor; Huan detested this and, on entering audience, spoke with passion of Zai's treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai assisted in government and, with the eunuch Dong Xiu, wove bonds to secure favor. Huan detested this and, on entering audience, spoke passionately of Zai's treachery.

sentences.zh: 代宗曰：「載雖非重慎，然協和中外無間然，能臣也。」

translations.literal: Daizong said: "Though Zai is not deeply cautious, yet he harmonizes inside and outside without friction—he is a capable minister."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong said, "Though Zai is not deeply cautious, he harmonizes court and realm without friction. He is a capable minister."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「和之為貴者，由禮節也，不節之以禮，焉得和？

translations.literal: He replied: "What makes harmony precious is ritual propriety; without restraining by ritual, how can there be harmony?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "What makes harmony precious is ritual propriety. Without restraining by ritual, how can there be harmony?

sentences.zh: 今幹戈甫定，品物思乂。

translations.literal: Now arms have just been laid down and all things long for order.
translations.idiomatic: Now arms have just been laid down and all things long for order.

sentences.zh: 載為宰相，宜明制度，易海內耳目。

translations.literal: As chief minister, Zai should clarify institutions and renew the ears and eyes of all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Zai should clarify institutions and renew the ears and eyes of the realm.

sentences.zh: 而怙權樹黨，毀法為通，鬻恩為恕，附下茍容，乃幽國卑主術，臣所未喻。」

translations.literal: Yet he relies on power and builds factions, destroys law to make passage, sells favor for indulgence, and attaches to inferiors with careless tolerance—the art of darkening the state and debasing the ruler—I do not understand it."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he relies on power and builds factions, destroys law to make passage, sells favor for indulgence, and attaches to inferiors with careless tolerance—the art of darkening the state and debasing the ruler. I do not understand it."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent.

sentences.zh: 會渙兼稅地青苗錢物使，以錢給百官，而吏用下直為使料，上直為百司料。

translations.literal: When Huan concurrently served as commissioner for green-sprout tax monies on taxed land, he used money to supply the hundred offices, while clerks used the lower rate for commissioner expenses and the higher rate for the hundred offices' supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan concurrently served as commissioner for green-sprout tax monies, he used money to supply the hundred offices, while clerks used the lower rate for commissioner expenses and the higher rate for the hundred offices' supplies.

sentences.zh: 載諷皇城副留守張清擿其非，詔尚書左丞蔣渙按實，且載所惡，由是貶道州刺史。

translations.literal: Zai prompted Deputy Defender of the Imperial City Zhang Qing to expose the fault; an edict ordered Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Jiang Huan to verify the facts—and since Jiang was whom Zai hated, Huan was therefore demoted to prefect of Dao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zai prompted Deputy Defender Zhang Qing to expose the fault. An edict ordered Left Vice Director Jiang Huan to verify the facts—and since Jiang was whom Zai hated, Huan was demoted to prefect of Dao.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太傅，謚曰元。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; his posthumous name was Yuan (Primary).
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; his posthumous name was Primary.

sentences.zh: 子縱。

translations.literal: His son Zong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zong.

sentences.zh: 縱繇協律郎三遷監察御史。

translations.literal: Zong rose from harmonics officer through three promotions to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zong rose from harmonics officer through three promotions to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 會詔擇令長，授藍田令，德化大行，縣人立碑頌德，渙之貶，縱棄金部員外郎就養。

translations.literal: When an edict chose magistrates and chiefs, he was made magistrate of Lantian; moral transformation was greatly practiced and the county people erected a stele praising his virtue. When Huan was demoted, Zong resigned as vice director of the gold office to support his father.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict chose magistrates, he was made magistrate of Lantian. Moral transformation flourished and the county people erected a stele praising his virtue. When Huan was demoted, Zong resigned as vice director of the gold office to support his father.

sentences.zh: 後為汴西水陸運、兩稅、鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: Later he was made commissioner for Bianxi water-and-land transport, two-tax, and salt-and-iron affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made commissioner for Bianxi water-and-land transport, two-tax, and salt-and-iron affairs.

sentences.zh: 王師圍田悅，乏食，詔縱餉四節度糧，軍無乏。

translations.literal: Imperial troops besieged Tian Yue but lacked food; an edict ordered Zong to supply grain to the four military commissioners, and the army wanted for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops besieged Tian Yue but lacked food. An edict ordered Zong to supply grain to the four military commissioners, and the army wanted for nothing.

sentences.zh: 德宗出奉天，方鎮兵未至。

translations.literal: Dezong went out to Fengtian; the frontier armies had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian; the frontier armies had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 縱勸李懷光奔命，悉軍財稱所須。

translations.literal: Zong urged Li Huai'guang to hurry to the emperor's call and supplied all army wealth as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Zong urged Li Huai'guang to hurry to the emperor's call and supplied all army wealth as needed.

sentences.zh: 懷光兵疲久戰，次河中，遷延不進。

translations.literal: Huai'guang's troops were weary from long fighting; he halted at Hezhong and delayed without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang's troops were weary from long fighting. He halted at Hezhong and delayed without advancing.

sentences.zh: 縱以金帛先度，曰：「濟者即賜。」

translations.literal: Zong sent gold and silk ahead, saying: "Whoever crosses shall receive reward at once."
translations.idiomatic: Zong sent gold and silk ahead, saying, "Whoever crosses shall receive reward at once."

sentences.zh: 眾趨利爭西，遂及奉天。

translations.literal: The masses rushed for profit and competed west, and thus reached Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The troops rushed for profit and competed west, and thus reached Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 上言：「懷光反覆不情，宜備之。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Huai'guang is fickle and faithless; he should be guarded against."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Huai'guang is fickle and faithless. He should be guarded against."

sentences.zh: 及帝徙梁州，追扈不及，左右短縱素善懷光，殆不來。

translations.literal: When the emperor moved to Liang Prefecture, Zong could not catch up in escort; those at the emperor's side slandered Zong as always friendly with Huai'guang and said he would likely not come.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved to Liang Prefecture, Zong could not catch up in escort. Those at the emperor's side slandered Zong as always friendly with Huai'guang and said he would likely not come.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「知縱者，朕也，非爾輩所及。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The one who knows Zong is I—not something you people can match."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The one who knows Zong is I—not something you can match."

sentences.zh: 後數日至，授御史大夫。

translations.literal: Several days later he arrived and was appointed censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he arrived and was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 處大體，不急細事，獄訴付成僚屬而已。

translations.literal: He handled great principles and did not press small matters; lawsuits he left to subordinate officials to complete.
translations.idiomatic: He handled great principles and did not press small matters; lawsuits he left to subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 自兵興，內外官冗溢，時議並省。

translations.literal: Since the rise of arms, offices inside and outside were redundant and overflowing; the age discussed merging and reducing them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rise of arms, offices inside and outside were redundant; the age discussed merging and reducing them.

sentences.zh: 縱奏：「兵未息，仕進者之緒，在官則累遷，有功而褒賞，不可廢也。

translations.literal: Zong memorialized: "Arms have not ceased; the thread of those advancing in office—while in office they are promoted in succession, and merit is rewarded—cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zong memorialized, "Arms have not ceased. The thread of advancement for officials—while in office they are promoted in succession, and merit is rewarded—cannot be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 比選集，乃據闕留人，怨望滋結。

translations.literal: Lately at selection gatherings they have held people according to vacancies; resentment and longing grow ever more tangled.
translations.idiomatic: Lately at selection gatherings they hold people according to vacancies; resentment grows ever more tangled.

sentences.zh: 朝廷頻詔錄勞，而諸道敘優日廣。

translations.literal: The court frequently edicts recording merit, while the circuits daily widen preferential rankings.
