translations.idiomatic: The court frequently records merit, while the circuits daily widen preferential rankings.

sentences.zh: 若停減吏員，非但承優者無官可敘，亦恐序進者無路勝置矣。」

translations.literal: If clerk numbers are halted and reduced, not only will those receiving preferential treatment have no office to be ranked in, but I also fear those advancing in order will have no place to be set."
translations.idiomatic: If clerk numbers are reduced, not only will those receiving preferential treatment have no office to be ranked in, but those advancing in order will have no place to be set."

sentences.zh: 詔可貞元元年，天子郊見，為大禮使。

translations.literal: The edict approved. In the first year of Zhenyuan the Son of Heaven performed suburban audience; Zong was made commissioner of great rites.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved. In Zhenyuan 1 (785) the Son of Heaven performed suburban audience; Zong was made commissioner of great rites.

sentences.zh: 歲旱用屈，縱撙裁文物，儉而不陋。

translations.literal: The year was drought-stricken and resources strained; Zong economized and trimmed ritual objects—frugal yet not shabby.
translations.idiomatic: The year was drought-stricken and resources strained. Zong economized and trimmed ritual objects—frugal yet not shabby.

sentences.zh: 除吏部侍郎，尋為河南尹。

translations.literal: He was made vice minister of civil office and soon became metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of civil office and soon became metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時兵雖定，民雕耗，縱治簡易，蠲略細苛。

translations.literal: Though arms were settled, the people were worn and depleted; Zong governed with simplicity and ease, remitting and omitting petty harshness.
translations.idiomatic: Though arms were settled, the people were worn and depleted. Zong governed with simplicity and ease, remitting petty harshness.

sentences.zh: 先是戍邊者道由洛，儲餼取於民。

translations.literal: Earlier, frontier garrison troops passed through Luo on the road; stored provisions were taken from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, frontier garrison troops passed through Luo; stored provisions were taken from the people.

sentences.zh: 縱始令官辦，使五家相保，自占發斂，以絕胥史之私。

translations.literal: Zong first ordered official provision, had five households mutually guarantee one another, and let them assess and collect themselves, to cut off clerks' private gain.
translations.idiomatic: Zong first ordered official provision, had five households mutually guarantee one another, and let them assess and collect themselves, to cut off clerks' private gain.

sentences.zh: 又引伊、洛溉高仰，通利裏闬，人甚宜之。

translations.literal: He also drew the Yi and Luo to irrigate the high uplands, benefiting lanes and wards; the people found it very suitable.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew the Yi and Luo to irrigate the high uplands, benefiting lanes and wards; the people found it very suitable.

sentences.zh: 入為太常卿，封常山縣公。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as minister of imperial sacrifices and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan County.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as minister of imperial sacrifices and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan County.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十二，贈吏部尚書，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-two, was posthumously made minister of civil office, and his posthumous name was Zhong (Loyal).
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two, was posthumously made Minister of Civil Office, and his posthumous name was Loyal.

sentences.zh: 初，渙為元載所抑，縱訖載世，不求聞達。

translations.literal: Earlier Huan had been suppressed by Yuan Zai; through Zai's age Zong did not seek fame or advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Huan had been suppressed by Yuan Zai. Through Zai's age Zong did not seek fame or advancement.

sentences.zh: 渙有嬖妾，縱以母事之。

translations.literal: Huan had a favored concubine; Zong treated her as a mother.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had a favored concubine; Zong treated her as a mother.

sentences.zh: 妾剛酷，雖縱顯官而數笞詬，然率妻子候顏色，承養不懈，時以為難。

translations.literal: The concubine was harsh and cruel; though Zong was a prominent official she often flogged and reviled him, yet he led wife and children to watch her expression and support her without slackening—the age considered it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The concubine was harsh and cruel. Though Zong was a prominent official she often flogged and reviled him, yet he led wife and children to watch her expression and support her without slackening—the age considered it difficult.

sentences.zh: 孫碣。

translations.literal: His grandson Jie.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Jie.

sentences.zh: 碣，字東標，及進士第，遷右拾遺。

translations.literal: Jie, styled Dongbiao, passed the jinshi examination and was transferred to right remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, courtesy name Dongbiao, passed the jinshi examination and was transferred to right remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 武宗方討澤潞，碣建請納劉稹降，忤旨，貶鄧城令。

translations.literal: When Wuzong was attacking Ze and Lu, Jie memorialized asking to accept Liu Zhen's surrender; offending the intent, he was demoted to magistrate of Dengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong was attacking Ze and Lu, Jie memorialized asking to accept Liu Zhen's surrender. Offending the throne, he was demoted to magistrate of Dengcheng.

sentences.zh: 稍轉商州刺史。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to prefect of Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually transferred to prefect of Shang.

sentences.zh: 擢河南尹、右散騎常侍，再為河南尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to metropolitan governor of Henan and right regular attendant, then again made metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to metropolitan governor of Henan and right regular attendant, then again made metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 邑有大賈王可久，轉貨江、湖間。

translations.literal: In the district was a great merchant Wang Kejiu, who traded goods between the Yangtze and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: In the district was a great merchant Wang Kejiu, who traded goods between the Yangtze and the lakes.

sentences.zh: 值龐勛亂，盡亡其貲，不得歸。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun's rebellion occurred, he lost all his wealth and could not return.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun's rebellion occurred, he lost all his wealth and could not return.

sentences.zh: 妻詣卜者楊乾夫咨在亡。

translations.literal: His wife went to the diviner Yang Qianfu to consult on whether he was alive or dead.
translations.idiomatic: His wife went to the diviner Yang Qianfu to ask whether he was alive or dead.

sentences.zh: 乾夫名善數，而內悅妻色，且利其富。

translations.literal: Qianfu was famed for skill in numbers, yet inwardly he delighted in the wife's beauty and also coveted her wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfu was famed for skill in divination, yet inwardly he delighted in the wife's beauty and coveted her wealth.

sentences.zh: 既占，陽驚曰：「乃夫殆不還矣！」

translations.literal: After divining, he feigned alarm: "Your husband will likely not return!"
translations.idiomatic: After divining, he feigned alarm: "Your husband will likely not return!"

sentences.zh: 即陰以百金謝媒者，誘聘之，妻乃嫁乾夫，遂為富人。

translations.literal: He secretly gave a hundred in gold to the matchmaker, enticed her into marriage, and the wife then married Qianfu and he became a rich man.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly gave a hundred in gold to the matchmaker, enticed her into marriage, and the wife married Qianfu, who thus became a rich man.

sentences.zh: 它年徐州平，可久困甚，丐衣食歸閭裏，往見妻。

translations.literal: Another year, when Xuzhou was pacified, Kejiu was extremely destitute, begged food and clothing, returned to his village, and went to see his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Another year, when Xuzhou was pacified, Kejiu was extremely destitute, begged food and clothing, returned to his village, and went to see his wife.

sentences.zh: 乾夫大怒，詬逐之。

translations.literal: Qianfu was greatly angered, reviled him, and drove him away.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfu was furious, reviled him, and drove him away.

sentences.zh: 妻詣吏自言，乾夫厚納賄，可久反得罪。

translations.literal: The wife went to officials and spoke for herself; Qianfu heavily bribed them, and Kejiu instead was found guilty.
translations.idiomatic: The wife went to officials and spoke for herself. Qianfu heavily bribed them, and Kejiu was found guilty instead.

sentences.zh: 再訴，復坐誣。

translations.literal: Appealing again, he was again convicted of false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Appealing again, he was again convicted of false accusation.

sentences.zh: 可久恨嘆，遂失明。

translations.literal: Kejiu hated and sighed, and thereafter went blind.
translations.idiomatic: Kejiu grieved and sighed, and thereafter went blind.

sentences.zh: 碣之來，可久陳冤，碣得其情，即敕吏掩乾夫並前獄史下獄，悉發賕奸，一日殺之，以妻還可久。

translations.literal: When Jie came, Kejiu stated his grievance; Jie got the facts, immediately ordered officials to seize Qianfu and the previous prison clerks and put them in jail, fully exposed their bribery and treachery, killed them in one day, and returned the wife to Kejiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie came, Kejiu stated his grievance. Jie got the facts, immediately ordered officials to seize Qianfu and the previous prison clerks, fully exposed their bribery and treachery, killed them in one day, and returned the wife to Kejiu.

sentences.zh: 時淫潦，獄決而霽，都民相語，歌舞於道。

translations.literal: At the time there was heavy flooding; when the case was decided the sky cleared, and capital people spoke to one another and sang and danced in the roads.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was heavy flooding. When the case was decided the sky cleared, and the people of the capital sang and danced in the roads.

sentences.zh: 徙陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to investigating commissioner of Shan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to investigating commissioner of Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 軍亂，貶懷州司馬，卒。

translations.literal: When the army mutinied, he was demoted to military commissioner of Huai Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the army mutinied, he was demoted to military commissioner of Huai and died.

sentences.zh: 張柬之，字孟將，襄州襄陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianzhi, styled Mengjiang, was a native of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi, courtesy name Mengjiang, was from Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少涉經史，補太學生。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the classics and histories and was appointed a student of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied the classics and histories and was appointed a student of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 祭酒令狐德棻異其才，便以王佐期之。

translations.literal: Director Linghu Defen regarded his talent as extraordinary and expected him to become a royal assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Director Linghu Defen regarded his talent as extraordinary and expected him to become a royal assistant.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，始調清源丞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was first assigned as assistant magistrate of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was first assigned as assistant magistrate of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，以賢良召，時年七十餘矣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang he was summoned as worthy and good; he was then over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchang 1 (689) he was summoned as worthy and good; he was then over seventy.

sentences.zh: 對策者千餘，柬之為第一。

translations.literal: More than a thousand answered policy questions; Jianzhi ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand answered policy questions. Jianzhi ranked first.

sentences.zh: 授監察御史，遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor and transferred to attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor and transferred to attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時突厥默啜有女請和親，武後欲令武延秀娶之。

translations.literal: At that time Mo-chuo of the Turks had a daughter who requested a marriage alliance, and Empress Wu wished to have Wu Yanxiu marry her.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Turkic khan Mo-chuo had a daughter who sought a marriage alliance, and Empress Wu wanted Wu Yanxiu to marry her.

sentences.zh: 柬之奏：「古無天子取夷狄女者。」

translations.literal: Jianzhi memorialized: "In antiquity there was never a Son of Heaven who took a barbarian woman's hand in marriage."
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi submitted a memorial: "Since antiquity no Son of Heaven has ever taken a barbarian woman in marriage."

sentences.zh: 忤旨，出為合、蜀二州刺史。

translations.literal: Having offended the imperial will, he was sent out as prefect of He and Shu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Having offended her, he was demoted to prefect of He and Shu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 故事，歲以兵五百戍姚州，地險瘴，到屯輒死。

translations.literal: By established practice, five hundred troops were garrisoned at Yao Prefecture each year; the terrain was treacherous and malarial, and men died as soon as they reached the post.
translations.idiomatic: By long-standing custom, five hundred soldiers were posted to Yao Prefecture every year. The land was rugged and pestilential, and men died as soon as they arrived.

sentences.zh: 柬之論其弊曰：

translations.literal: Jianzhi discussed the harm of this, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi analyzed the abuses and said:

sentences.zh: 臣按姚州，古哀牢國，域土荒外，山岨水深。

translations.literal: Your subject has examined Yao Prefecture: it was the ancient kingdom of Ailao, its territory lying beyond the wild frontier, its mountains steep and its waters deep.
translations.idiomatic: I have reviewed the case of Yao Prefecture. It was the ancient kingdom of Ailao, a land beyond the frontier wilds where mountains rise steeply and rivers run deep.

sentences.zh: 漢世未與中國通，唐蒙開夜郎、滇笮，而哀牢不附。

translations.literal: In Han times it had no contact with China; Tang Meng opened Yelang and Dian/Zuo, yet Ailao did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times it had no ties with the central realm. Tang Meng opened Yelang and Dian and Zuo, but Ailao still refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 東漢光武末，始請內屬，置永昌郡統之。

translations.literal: At the end of Eastern Han under Emperor Guangwu, it first requested to become an internal dependency, and Yongchang Commandery was established to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the end of Eastern Han under Emperor Guangwu did it ask to come under direct rule, and Yongchang Commandery was created to govern it.

sentences.zh: 賦其鹽布氈罽以利中土。

translations.literal: Its salt, cloth, felt, and rugs were levied as tribute to benefit the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: Salt, cloth, felt, and rugs were taxed from it for the profit of the heartland.

sentences.zh: 其國西大秦，南交趾，奇珍之貢不闕。

translations.literal: Its country bordered Great Qin to the west and Jiaozhi to the south, and tribute of rare treasures was never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The region lay west of Daqin and south of Jiaozhi, and tribute of rare goods never ceased.

sentences.zh: 劉備據蜀，甲兵不充，諸葛亮五月度瀘，收其產入以益軍，使張伯岐選取勁兵，以增武備。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei held Shu, his armor and troops were insufficient; in the fifth month Zhuge Liang crossed the Lu River, gathered its produce for the army's supply, and had Zhang Boqi select strong soldiers to augment the military stores.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei held Shu and his forces were understrength, Zhuge Liang crossed the Lu River in the fifth month, drew on local produce to supply the army, and had Zhang Boqi recruit strong troops to strengthen the military.

sentences.zh: 故《蜀志》稱亮南征後，國以富饒。

translations.literal: Hence the Chronicle of Shu states that after Liang's southern campaign, the state grew rich.
translations.idiomatic: The Chronicle of Shu therefore says that after Liang's southern expedition the state became prosperous.

sentences.zh: 此前世置郡，以其利之也。

translations.literal: This is why previous dynasties established commanderies there—for the profit to be had.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynasties established commanderies there precisely because of such profit.

sentences.zh: 今鹽布之稅不供，珍奇之貢不入，戈戟之用不實於戎行，賨貨之資不輸於大國。

translations.literal: Now the salt-and-cloth taxes are not delivered, rare tribute does not arrive, spears and halberds do not fill the ranks, and riches do not flow to the great state.
translations.idiomatic: Today the salt-and-cloth levies are not paid, rare tribute does not come in, weapons do not reach the armies, and wealth does not reach the empire.

sentences.zh: 而空竭府庫，驅率平人，受役蠻夷，肝腦塗地。

translations.literal: Yet the treasury is emptied for naught, common people are driven forth, and they suffer forced service under the barbarians, their flesh and blood staining the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the treasury is drained for nothing, common people are driven away, and they are forced to serve the barbarians until their flesh and blood cover the earth.

sentences.zh: 臣竊為陛下惜之。

translations.literal: Your subject privately grieves this on Your Majesty's account.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot help grieving over this for Your Majesty's sake.

sentences.zh: 昔漢歷博南山，涉蘭倉水，更置博南、哀牢二縣。

translations.literal: Formerly Han traversed Mount Bonan, crossed the Lancang waters, and newly established Bonan and Ailao counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Han crossed Mount Bonan and the Lancang River and then set up Bonan and Ailao counties.

sentences.zh: 蜀人愁苦，行者作歌曰：「歷博南，越蘭津，度蘭倉，為他人。」

translations.literal: The people of Shu were anguished, and travelers made a song: "Crossing Bonan, fording Lanjin, passing Lancang—for others' sake."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu were wretched, and travelers sang: "Crossing Bonan, fording Lanjin, passing Lancang—all for someone else."

sentences.zh: 蓋譏其貪珍奇之利，而為蠻夷所驅役也。

translations.literal: This mocked their greed for rare treasures while being driven as servants by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The song mocked those who coveted rare goods yet ended up driven like servants by the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 漢獲其利，人且怨歌。

translations.literal: Han gained profit from it, yet the people sang songs of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Han took the profit, and still the people sang in resentment.

sentences.zh: 今減耗國儲，費調日引，使陛下赤子身膏野草，骸骨不歸，老母幼子哀號望祭於千里之外。

translations.literal: Now the state stores are depleted, expenses and levies daily increase, causing Your Majesty's own children to feed the wild grasses—their bones never returning, old mothers and young children wailing and making offerings from a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Now the state's reserves are drained and levies grow daily, so that Your Majesty's own people feed the wild grass—their bones never return home, and old mothers and young children wail and make offerings a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 朝廷無絲發利，而百姓蒙終身之酷，臣竊為國家痛之。

translations.literal: The court gains not a thread of benefit, while the people suffer a lifetime of cruelty; your subject privately grieves for the state on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: The court receives not the slightest gain, while the people endure lifelong misery. I cannot help mourning this for the state.

sentences.zh: 往諸葛亮破南中，即用渠率統之，不置漢官，不留戍兵。

translations.literal: In the past when Zhuge Liang conquered the southern middle, he immediately used local chieftains to govern it, established no Han officials, and left no garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang conquered the southern middle in the past, he at once put local chieftains in charge, appointed no Han officials, and left no garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 言置官留兵有三不易：置官必夷漢雜居，猜嫌將起；

translations.literal: He said that establishing officials and leaving troops had three difficulties: establishing officials would inevitably mix Yi and Han in residence, and suspicion and resentment would arise;
translations.idiomatic: He said that appointing officials and leaving troops had three drawbacks: officials would force Yi and Han to live together and breed suspicion and strife;

sentences.zh: 留兵轉糧，為患滋重；

translations.literal: keeping troops would require grain transport, making the harm ever worse;
translations.idiomatic: keeping troops would mean hauling grain and would only deepen the harm;

sentences.zh: 後忽反叛，勞費必甚。

translations.literal: if they rebelled later, the labor and expense would surely be immense.
translations.idiomatic: and if rebellion came later, the cost in labor and treasure would be enormous.

sentences.zh: 故粗設綱紀，自然久定。

translations.literal: Thus he only set out basic regulations, and naturally lasting stability followed.
translations.idiomatic: So he laid down only broad rules, and order lasted of itself.

sentences.zh: 臣謂亮之策，誠盡羈縻蠻夷之要。

translations.literal: Your subject considers Liang's policy the true essence of keeping the barbarians bridled and attached.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Liang's policy truly grasped the heart of keeping the barbarians restrained and loyal.

sentences.zh: 今姚州官屬，即無固邊厭寇之心，又無亮且縱且擒之伎。

translations.literal: Today's Yao Prefecture officials neither possess the will to secure the border and subdue enemies, nor Liang's skill of releasing and capturing in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Today's officials at Yao Prefecture have neither the will to hold the frontier and repel invaders nor Liang's art of loosening and tightening control in turn.

sentences.zh: 唯詭謀狡算，恣情割剝；

translations.literal: They only scheming conspiracies and cunning calculations, indulging in extortion at will;
translations.idiomatic: They know only secret plots and cunning schemes, and plunder as they please;

sentences.zh: 扇動酋渠，遣成朋常：折支諂笑，取媚蠻夷，拜跪趨伏，無復為恥；

translations.literal: They incite tribal chiefs and foster cliques and faction: bowing and scraping with flattery, courting the barbarians' favor, kneeling and prostrating themselves without any sense of shame;
translations.idiomatic: they stir up tribal leaders and form factions: cringing and flattering to please the barbarians, kneeling and groveling without a trace of shame;

sentences.zh: 提挈子弟，嘯引兇愚，聚會蒲博，一擲累萬。

translations.literal: They drag along their sons and younger brothers, summon the violent and foolish, gather for gambling, and stake tens of thousands in a single throw.
translations.idiomatic: they drag in sons and younger brothers, rally the violent and foolish, gather to gamble, and stake tens of thousands on a single throw.

sentences.zh: 凡逋逃亡命在彼州者，戶贏二千，專事剽奪。

translations.literal: All fugitives who had fled for their lives in that prefecture numbered over two thousand households, devoting themselves solely to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Every fugitive who had taken refuge there numbered more than two thousand households, all devoted to robbery.

sentences.zh: 且姚州本龍朔中武陵主簿石子仁奏置，其後長史李孝讓、辛文協死於群蠻，詔遣郎將趙武貴討擊，兵無噍類，又以將軍李義總繼往，而郎將劉惠基戰死，其州遂廢。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yao Prefecture was originally established on a memorial from Wuling chief clerk Shi Ziren in the Longshuo era; later the chief minister Li Xiaorang and Xin Wenxie died at the hands of the barbarian hordes; an edict dispatched General Zhao Wugui to attack, and not a soldier survived; then General Li Yizong was sent in succession, but General Liu Huiji died in battle, and the prefecture was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Prefecture itself had been established on a memorial from Wuling chief clerk Shi Ziren in the Longshuo era. Later chief ministers Li Xiaorang and Xin Wenxie were killed by the barbarians. An edict sent General Zhao Wugui to punish them, and not one soldier returned. General Li Yizong was sent next, but General Liu Huiji died in battle, and the prefecture was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以亮有三不易，其言卒驗。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that Liang's three points of difficulty were in the end borne out.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Liang's three warnings were proved in the end.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，蠻郎將王善寶、昆州刺史爨乾福復請置州，言課稅自支，不旁取於蜀。

translations.literal: During the Chuigong era, barbarian commander Wang Shanbao and Kun Prefecture inspector Cuan Qianfu again requested establishment of the prefecture, saying its taxes would support itself without drawing on Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chuigong era, barbarian commander Wang Shanbao and Kun Prefecture inspector Cuan Qianfu again asked that the prefecture be restored, claiming its revenues would support itself without burdening Shu.

sentences.zh: 及置，州掾李棱為蠻所殺。

translations.literal: Once it was established, the prefectural aide Li Ling was killed by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as it was reestablished, the prefectural aide Li Ling was killed by the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 延載中，司馬成琛更置瀘南七鎮，戍以蜀兵，蜀始擾矣。

translations.literal: During the Yanzai era, the military governor Cheng Chen newly established seven forts south of Lu, garrisoned with Shu troops, and Shu began to be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanzai era, military governor Cheng Chen set up seven forts south of the Lu River and garrisoned them with Shu troops, and Shu began to suffer unrest.

sentences.zh: 且姚府總管五十七州間，皆巨猾遊客。

translations.literal: Moreover, among the fifty-seven prefectures under Yao Prefecture's general supervision, all were great scoundrels and wandering adventurers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among the fifty-seven prefectures under the Yao superintendency, nearly all were great rogues and drifting adventurers.

sentences.zh: 國家設官，所以正俗防奸，而無恥之吏，敗謬至此。

translations.literal: The state establishes officials to rectify custom and guard against wrongdoing, yet these shameless officers have brought ruin to this point.
translations.idiomatic: The state appoints officials to set customs right and guard against wrongdoing, yet these shameless officers have brought affairs to such ruin.

sentences.zh: 今劫害未止，恐驚擾之禍日滋。

translations.literal: Now plunder and harm have not ceased; I fear the calamity of disturbance will daily grow.
translations.idiomatic: Robbery and violence have not stopped, and I fear the harm of unrest will grow day by day.

sentences.zh: 宜罷姚州，隸巂府，歲時朝覲同蕃國；

translations.literal: Yao Prefecture should be abolished and placed under Xi Prefecture, with annual court audience like foreign tributary states;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Prefecture should be abolished and placed under Xi Prefecture, with annual audiences like those of tributary states;

sentences.zh: 廢瀘南諸鎮，而設關瀘北，非命使，不許交通；

translations.literal: the forts south of Lu should be abolished and passes established north of Lu, with no traffic permitted except by imperial commission;
translations.idiomatic: the forts south of the Lu should be dismantled and checkpoints set up north of the Lu, with no travel allowed except by imperial envoy;

sentences.zh: 增巂屯兵，擇清良吏以統之。

translations.literal: garrison troops at Xi should be increased, and upright officials chosen to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: garrison troops at Xi should be increased, and upright officials chosen to command them.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為便。

translations.literal: Your subject deems this expedient.
translations.idiomatic: I believe this would be the wise course.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 俄為荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Soon he became chief minister of the Jingzhou Grand Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made chief minister of the Jingzhou Grand Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 長安中，武後謂狄仁傑曰：「安得一奇士用之？」

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, Empress Wu said to Di Renjie: "How can I obtain an extraordinary man to employ?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era, Empress Wu said to Di Renjie, "Where can I find an extraordinary man to use?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「陛下求文章資歷，今宰相李嶠、蘇味道足矣。

translations.literal: Renjie said: "If Your Majesty seeks literary talent and credentials, the current chancellors Li Jiao and Su Weidao suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "If Your Majesty wants literary talent and senior credentials, the current chancellors Li Jiao and Su Weidao are enough.

sentences.zh: 豈文士齷齪，不足與成天下務哉？」

translations.literal: Are literary men so narrow-minded they cannot accomplish the affairs of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Are literary men so petty that they cannot handle the affairs of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 後曰「然。」

translations.literal: The Empress said, "True."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "True."

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：荊州長史張柬之雖老，宰相材也。

translations.literal: Renjie said: "Though Jing Prefecture chief minister Zhang Jianzhi is old, he has the makings of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "Zhang Jianzhi, chief minister of Jing Prefecture, is old, but he has the makings of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 用之必盡節於國。」

translations.literal: Employ him and he will surely exhaust his loyalty for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Use him, and he will give his utmost loyalty to the state."

sentences.zh: 即召為洛州司馬。

translations.literal: He was immediately summoned as Lu Prefecture vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi was at once summoned and made vice prefect of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 它日又求人，仁傑曰：「臣嘗薦張柬之，未用也。」

translations.literal: Another day she sought a man again; Renjie said: "Your subject once recommended Zhang Jianzhi, but he was not employed."
translations.idiomatic: Another day she asked for a man again. Renjie said, "I once recommended Zhang Jianzhi, but he was not used."

sentences.zh: 後曰：「遷之矣。」

translations.literal: The Empress said: "He has been transferred."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "He has been transferred."

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣薦宰相而為司馬，非用也。」

translations.literal: He said: "Your subject recommended a chancellor, yet he was made vice prefect—that is not employment."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I recommended a chancellor, yet he was made a vice prefect. That is not using him."

sentences.zh: 乃授司刑少卿，遷秋官侍郎。

translations.literal: Then he was made vice minister of justice and transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi was then made vice minister of justice and promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 後姚崇為靈武軍使，將行，後詔舉外司可為相者，崇曰：「張柬之沈厚有謀，能斷大事，其人老，惟亟用之。」

translations.literal: Later, when Yao Chong was made commissioner of the Lingwu Army and was about to depart, the Empress ordered recommendations of outside officials who could serve as chancellor; Chong said: "Zhang Jianzhi is deep and steady with plans and can decide great affairs; the man is old—only employ him at once."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yao Chong was appointed commissioner of the Lingwu Army and was about to leave, the Empress ordered recommendations of outside officials fit to be chancellor. Chong said, "Zhang Jianzhi is steady and resourceful and can decide great matters. He is old, and Your Majesty must use him quickly."

sentences.zh: 即日召見，拜同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，進鳳閣侍郎。

translations.literal: That same day he was summoned for audience, appointed Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Secretariat, and promoted to Phoenix Pavilion vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Jianzhi was summoned to audience, made Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Secretariat, and promoted to vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 誅二張也，柬之首發其謀。

translations.literal: In the execution of the Two Zhangs, Jianzhi was the first to initiate the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When the Two Zhangs were executed, Jianzhi was the first to set the plot in motion.

sentences.zh: 以功擢天官尚書、同鳳閣鸞臺三品、漢陽郡公，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, Same Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Third Rank, Duke of Hanyang, with a fief of five hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Personnel, given the third rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Secretariat, made Duke of Hanyang, and granted a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 不半歲，以漢陽郡王加特進，罷政事。

translations.literal: Within half a year he was made Prince of Hanyang with special advancement and removed from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In less than half a year he was made Prince of Hanyang with special advancement and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 柬之既失權，願還襄州養疾，乃授襄州刺史。

translations.literal: Having lost power, Jianzhi wished to return to Xiang Prefecture to convalesce and was appointed prefect of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jianzhi lost power, he asked to return to Xiang Prefecture to recover his health and was appointed its prefect.

sentences.zh: 中宗為賦詩祖道，又詔群臣餞定鼎門外。

translations.literal: Zhongzong composed a farewell poem for his send-off and also ordered the ministers to see him off outside the Dingding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong wrote a farewell poem for his departure and ordered the ministers to give him a send-off outside the Dingding Gate.

sentences.zh: 至州，持下以法，雖親舊無所縱貸，會漢水漲嚙城郭，柬之因壘為堤，以遏湍怒，闔境賴之。

translations.literal: Arriving at the prefecture, he upheld the law without favor even to relatives and old friends; when the Han River rose and eroded the walls, Jianzhi built embankments to check the raging flood, and the entire region relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: At the prefecture he enforced the law without exception, even for relatives and old friends. When the Han River swelled and gnawed at the walls, Jianzhi built dikes to hold back the raging waters, and the whole region depended on him.

sentences.zh: 又墾辭王爵，不許。

translations.literal: He again earnestly petitioned to decline the princely title, but it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He again petitioned to decline the princely title, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 俄及貶，又流瀧州，憂憤卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: Soon he was demoted and then exiled to Long Prefecture; he died of grief and indignation at eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted and exiled to Long Prefecture, where he died of grief and anger at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，贈中書令，謚曰文貞，授一子官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun he was posthumously made Palatine Secretary, given the posthumous name Wen Zhen (Cultured and Upright), and one son was granted office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingyun he was posthumously made Palatine Secretary, given the posthumous name Cultured and Upright, and one son was granted an official post.

sentences.zh: 柬之剛直不傅會，然邃於學，論次書數十篇。

translations.literal: Jianzhi was upright and would not curry favor, yet was deeply learned and authored dozens of treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi was upright and refused to trim his views to please others, yet he was deeply learned and wrote several dozen treatises.

sentences.zh: 子願、漪。

translations.literal: His sons were Yuan and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yuan and Yi.

sentences.zh: 願仕至襄州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan rose to prefect of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan rose to become prefect of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 漪以著作佐郎侍父襄陽，恃其家立功，簡接鄉人，鄉人怨之。

translations.literal: Yi served his father at Xiangyang as assistant compiler; relying on his family's merit, he treated fellow villagers with condescension, and they resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served his father at Xiangyang as assistant compiler. Trusting in his family's achievements, he treated local people with casual disdain, and they resented him.

sentences.zh: 初，易之等誅後，中宗猶監國告武氏廟，而天久陰不霽。

translations.literal: Initially, after the Zhang brothers were executed, Zhongzong still supervised the realm and reported to the Wu family temple, while the sky remained overcast for a long time without clearing.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after the Zhang brothers were executed, Zhongzong still governed as regent and reported to the Wu family temple, while the sky stayed overcast for many days.

sentences.zh: 侍御史崔渾奏「陛下復國，當正唐家位號，稱天下心。

translations.literal: Attending censor Cui Hun memorialized: "Your Majesty has restored the state; you should rectify the Tang house's titles to match the hearts of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Cui Hun submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty has restored the Tang state. You should restore the Tang house's titles and titles to win the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 奈何尚告武氏廟？

translations.literal: Why still report to the Wu family temple?
translations.idiomatic: Why still report to the Wu family temple?

sentences.zh: 請毀之，復唐宗廟。」

translations.literal: I ask that it be destroyed and the Tang ancestral temple restored."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that it be destroyed and the Tang ancestral temple restored."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 是日詔書下，翳澄駁，鹹以為天人之應。

translations.literal: That day when the edict was issued, the overcast sky cleared, and all regarded it as a correspondence between Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the edict was issued, the long overcast cleared, and everyone took it as Heaven and man responding in accord.

sentences.zh: 袁恕己，滄州東光人。

translations.literal: Yuan Shuji was a native of Dongguang in Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shuji was from Dongguang in Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仕累司刑少卿，知相王府司馬。

translations.literal: Through successive appointments he rose to vice minister of justice and served as military adjutant of the Prince of Xiang's household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to vice minister of justice and served as adjutant of the Prince of Xiang's household.

sentences.zh: 與誅二張，又從相王統南衙兵備非常，以功加銀青光祿大夫、中書侍郎、同中書門下三品，封南陽郡公，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: He joined in executing the Two Zhangs and then followed the Prince of Xiang in commanding the southern palace guard against emergency; for his merit he was given the silver-blue-glowing grand master of splendid happiness, made vice director of the Secretariat, Same Secretariat and Chancellery Third Rank, enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang, with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in executing the Two Zhangs and then followed the Prince of Xiang in commanding the southern palace guard against emergency. For his service he was given the silver-blue-glowing grand master of splendid happiness, made vice director of the Secretariat, given third rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang, and granted a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 將作少匠楊務廉者，以工巧進。

translations.literal: Chief artisan of the Directorate of Palace Buildings Yang Wulian advanced through craftsmanship and ingenuity.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wulian, chief artisan of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, rose through skill and ingenuity.

sentences.zh: 恕己恐其復啟遊娛侈麗之漸，言於中宗曰：「務廉位九卿，忠言嘉謨不聞，而專事營構以媚上，不斥之，亡以昭德。」

translations.literal: Shuji feared he would again open the way toward pleasure-seeking and extravagant display, and said to Zhongzong: "Wulian holds rank among the nine ministers, yet no loyal words or fine counsel are heard from him; he devotes himself solely to construction to flatter superiors—if he is not dismissed, virtue cannot be displayed."
translations.idiomatic: Shuji feared Yang would again lead the court toward pleasure and extravagant building. He told Zhongzong, "Wulian holds one of the nine ministerial posts, yet we hear no loyal counsel from him. He devotes himself to construction to please his superiors. If he is not removed, there is no way to show what virtue demands."

sentences.zh: 乃授陵州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then appointed prefect of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was then appointed prefect of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜中書令、特進、南陽郡王，罷政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Palatine Secretary, specially advanced, Prince of Nanyang, and removed from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Palatine Secretary, given special advancement, made Prince of Nanyang, and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 例及貶，又流環州，為周利貞所逼，恕己素餌黃金。

translations.literal: When the precedent of demotion reached him, he was further exiled to Huan Prefecture and was pressed by Zhou Lizhen; Shuji had long consumed gold.
translations.idiomatic: When the general demotion reached him, he was exiled further to Huan Prefecture and hounded by Zhou Lizhen. Shuji had long taken gold for longevity.

sentences.zh: 至是飲野葛數升，不死，憤懣，抔土以食，爪甲盡，不能絕，乃擊殺之。

translations.literal: At this he drank several sheng of wild-ge poison but did not die; in fury and anguish he ate handfuls of earth until his fingernails were gone, yet could not end his life, whereupon Zhou killed him by beating.
translations.idiomatic: He then drank several sheng of wild-ge poison but did not die. In rage and despair he ate handfuls of earth until his fingernails wore away, yet still could not die, and Zhou Lizhen beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 謚曰貞烈。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Zhenlie (Upright and Steadfast).
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Upright and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 孫高。

translations.literal: His grandson was Gao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Gao.

sentences.zh: 高字公頤。

translations.literal: Gao's courtesy name was Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, courtesy name Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 少慷慨有節尚。

translations.literal: From youth he was bold and principled.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was bold and principled.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 代宗時，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: During Emperor Daizong's reign he was repeatedly promoted to palace aide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Daizong he rose through successive promotions to palace aide.

sentences.zh: 建中中，拜京畿觀察使，坐累貶韶州長史，復拜給事中。

translations.literal: During the Jianzhong era he was made metropolitan circuit inspector, was demoted to chief minister of Shao Prefecture on account of offenses, then again made palace aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianzhong era he was made metropolitan circuit inspector, was demoted to chief minister of Shao Prefecture for offenses, and was later restored as palace aide.

sentences.zh: 德宗將起盧杞為饒州刺史，高當草詔，見宰相盧翰，劉從一曰：「杞當國。

translations.literal: When Dezong was about to recall Lu Qi as prefect of Rao, Gao was to draft the edict; he saw chancellors Lu Han and Liu Congyi and said: "When Qi held the state,
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong was about to appoint Lu Qi prefect of Rao, Gao was to draft the edict. He went to chancellors Lu Han and Liu Congyi and said, "When Lu Qi held power,

sentences.zh: 矯誣陰賊，斥忠誼，傲明德，反易天常，使宗祏失守，天下疣痏，朝廷不寘以法，才示貶黜，今還授大州，天下其謂何？」

translations.literal: he twisted truth and practiced secret villainy, drove out loyalty and righteousness, showed contempt for bright virtue, reversed Heaven's constant order, caused the ancestral temple to be lost, and left the realm covered in sores; the court did not punish him by law and only showed demotion—now he is again given a great prefecture; what will the realm say?"
translations.idiomatic: he twisted truth and practiced secret villainy, drove out the loyal and righteous, scorned bright virtue, overturned Heaven's order, left the ancestral temple undefended, and covered the realm in sores. The court did not punish him by law and only demoted him. Now he is given a great prefecture again—what will the world say?"

sentences.zh: 翰等不悅，命舍人作詔。

translations.literal: Han and the others were displeased and ordered an attendant to compose the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Han and the others were displeased and ordered an attendant to draft the edict instead.

sentences.zh: 詔出，高執不下，奏曰：「陛下用杞為相，出入三年，附下罔上，使陛下越在草莽，群臣願食其肉且不厭。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Gao held it and refused to promulgate it, memorializing: "When Your Majesty employed Qi as chancellor for three years, he fawned on subordinates and deceived superiors, causing Your Majesty to wander in the wilds; the ministers would devour his flesh and not be sated.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict came out, Gao held it back and refused to issue it. He memorialized: "When Your Majesty made Qi chancellor for three years, he fawned on subordinates and deceived superiors, driving Your Majesty into exile. The ministers would eat his flesh and still not be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 漢法，三光不有，雨旱不時，皆宰相請罪，小者免，大者戮。

translations.literal: By Han law, when the sun, moon, and stars are abnormal or rain and drought come untimely, the chancellor must request punishment—minor cases merit dismissal, major ones execution.
translations.idiomatic: By Han law, when the sun, moon, and stars are abnormal or rain and drought come at the wrong time, the chancellor must ask to be punished—lesser faults merit dismissal, greater ones death.

sentences.zh: 杞罪萬誅，陛下赦不誅，止貶新州，俄又內移，今復拜刺史，誠失天下望。」

translations.literal: Qi's crimes deserve ten thousand executions; Your Majesty pardoned without executing, only demoted him to Xin Prefecture, soon moved him inward again, and now again appoints him prefect—truly losing the hope of all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Qi's crimes deserved ten thousand deaths. Your Majesty spared him, demoted him only to Xin, soon brought him back inward, and now appoints him prefect again—truly forfeiting the world's trust."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「杞不逮，是朕之過。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Qi was not up to the task—that was my fault.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Qi was not up to the task—that was my fault.

sentences.zh: 朕已再赦。」

translations.literal: I have already pardoned him twice."
translations.idiomatic: I have already pardoned him twice."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「杞天資詭險，非不逮，彼固所餘。

translations.literal: He replied: "Qi was by nature deceitful and treacherous—not that he was inadequate; that was what remained in him.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Qi was by nature deceitful and treacherous—not that he was inadequate. That was his true nature.

sentences.zh: 赦者，止赦其罪，不宜授刺史。

translations.literal: A pardon only pardons the crime; he should not be given a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A pardon only pardons the crime; he should not be given a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 願問外廷，並敕中人聽於民。

translations.literal: I wish to ask the outer court, and also order eunuchs to listen among the people.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to ask the outer court, and also have eunuchs listen among the people.

sentences.zh: 若億兆異臣之言，臣請前死。」

translations.literal: If the hundred millions differ from your servant's words, your servant asks to die first."
translations.idiomatic: If the people disagree with me, I ask to die first."

sentences.zh: 諫官亦力爭帝前。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials also strove before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials also argued forcefully before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「與上佐可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Would making him a senior assistant be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Would making him a senior assistant be acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 群臣奉詔。

translations.literal: The ministers received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers received the edict.

sentences.zh: 翌日，遣使慰高曰：「朕惟卿言切至，已如奏。」

translations.literal: The next day he sent an envoy to comfort Gao, saying: "I consider your words urgent and sincere; it has been done as you memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent an envoy to comfort Gao, saying, "Your words were urgent and sincere; it has been done as you asked."

sentences.zh: 太子少保韋倫曰：「高言勁挺，自是陛下一良臣，宜加優禮。」

translations.literal: Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wei Lun said: "Gao's words are forceful and upright; he is by nature a good minister for Your Majesty and should receive added courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wei Lun said, "Gao's words are forceful and upright. He is a good minister for Your Majesty and should receive added courtesy."

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，帝以大盜後關輔百姓貧，田多荒茀，詔諸道上耕牛，委京兆府勸課。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, because after the great bandits the Guanfu people were poor and fields were largely overgrown, the emperor issued an edict that circuits send plow oxen and entrusted Jing Metropolitan Prefecture to encourage cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 (786), because after the great bandits the Guanfu people were poor and fields were largely overgrown, the emperor ordered circuits to send plow oxen and entrusted the Jing metropolitan prefecture to encourage cultivation.

sentences.zh: 量地給牛，不滿五十畝不給。

translations.literal: Land was measured to give oxen; those with less than fifty mu received none.
translations.idiomatic: Land was measured to distribute oxen; households with less than fifty mu received none.

sentences.zh: 高以為聖心所憂，乃在窮乏。

translations.literal: Gao held that what the sage heart worried over was poverty and want.
translations.idiomatic: Gao held that what the sage heart worried over was poverty and want.

sentences.zh: 今田不及五十畝即是窮人，請兩戶共給一牛。

translations.literal: Now those with fields under fifty mu are the poor; I beg that two households jointly receive one ox.
translations.idiomatic: Now those with fields under fifty mu are the poor. I beg that two households jointly receive one ox.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] complied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十，中外悵惜。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty; inside and outside the court grieved.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty; court and country grieved.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，李吉甫言其忠謇，特贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's time Li Jifu spoke of his loyalty and forthrightness, and he was specially posthumously made minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzong, Li Jifu spoke of his loyalty and forthrightness, and he was specially posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 文宗開成三年，又詔：玄暐曾孫郢為監察御史，暉曾孫元膺河南丞，柬之四世孫憬壽安尉，恕己曾孫德文校書郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng of Wenzong another edict stated: Xuanwei's great-great-grandson Ying was made investigating censor, Hui's great-great-grandson Yuanying Henan assistant prefect, Jianzhi's fourth-generation descendant Jing Shou'an commandant, and Shuji's great-great-grandson Dewen collation secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 3 (838) of Emperor Wenzong another edict appointed Xuanwei's great-great-grandson Ying investigating censor, Hui's great-great-grandson Yuanying assistant prefect of Henan, Jianzhi's fourth-generation descendant Jing commandant of Shou'an, and Shuji's great-great-grandson Dewen collation secretary.

sentences.zh: 始，帝訪御史中丞狄兼暮，以仁傑功，且言五王遺烈，乃求其後，秩以官。

translations.literal: At the beginning the emperor consulted Censor-in-Chief Di Jianmu; because of Di Renjie's merit and speaking also of the Five Kings' lingering glory, he sought their descendants and ranked them with offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning the emperor consulted Censor-in-Chief Di Jianmu. Because of Di Renjie's merit and the lingering glory of the Five Kings, he sought their descendants and granted them offices.

sentences.zh: 唯彥範後無聞云。

translations.literal: Only Yanfan's descendants were not heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanfan's descendants were not heard of.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：五王提衛兵誅嬖臣，中興唐室，不淹辰，天下晏然，其謀深矣。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The Five Kings led guard troops to execute favored ministers, revived the Tang house, and within a day the realm was tranquil—their plan was deep indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The Five Kings led guard troops to kill the emperor's favorites, revived the Tang house, and within a day the realm was tranquil—their plan was deep indeed.

sentences.zh: 至謂中宗為英王，不盡誅諸武，使天子藉以為威，何其淺耶？

translations.literal: Yet to say that because Zhongzong was Prince Ying they did not fully execute the Wu, leaving them for the Son of Heaven to use as leverage—how shallow!
translations.idiomatic: Yet to say that because Zhongzong had been Prince Ying they did not wipe out the Wu, leaving them for the emperor to use as leverage—how shallow!

sentences.zh: 釁牙一啟，為艷後，豎兒所乘，劫持戮辱，若放豚然，何哉？

translations.literal: Once the fang was bared, they were ridden by the voluptuous empress and by palace boys, seized, humiliated, and slaughtered like released pigs—why?
translations.idiomatic: Once the trap was sprung, they were ridden by the voluptuous empress and palace favorites, seized, humiliated, and slaughtered like pigs—why?

sentences.zh: 無亦神奪其明，厚韋氏毒，以興先天之業乎？

translations.literal: Was it not rather that the spirits stole their clarity, thickened the Wei clan's poison, to raise the enterprise of Xiantian?
translations.idiomatic: Was it not rather that Heaven stole their clarity, thickened the Wei clan's poison, to raise the enterprise of Xiantian?

sentences.zh: 不然，安李之功，賢於漢平、勃遠矣！

translations.literal: If not, the achievement of securing Li would have far surpassed Han's Ping and Bo!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, the achievement of securing the Li house would have far surpassed the Han ministers Ping and Bo!
